column23: ["OX: ANALYTIC AND DECISION SUPPORT TOOL ENABLING HUMAN-MACHINE LEARNING","Ox Intel is removing barriers to adoption of AI in human-led analysis and decision-making. As analysts and decision-makers suffer from information overload, there is substantial interest in leveraging next-generation technology such as ML to augment human capacities. However, traditional human-led decision-making and analytic processes have presented barriers to adoption of next-generation technology. Current decision-making and analytical processes are unstructured, inconsistent, and opaque; they waste time and energy, allocating tasks to people that could be performed more efficiently and accurately by machines; and they fail to collect essential data around past judgments to improve future analysis. This creates a major opportunity cost and competitive disadvantage, both for the Defense community and other sectors. Ox bolsters the analytical judgment-making process—an essential area entirely underserved by available technology, and an area where crucial human qualities and capabilities are at risk of being displaced by “black box” automated processes.  Ox is a web-based SaaS platform that leverages structured analytic techniques to structure data around human judgments, enforcing rigor, consistency, and transparency. In the Ox platform, users capture their analytical and decision-making criteria for a range of use cases. Ox then provides a consistent and transparent scoring mechanism for analytic confidence, and enables users to track the performance of their assessments. Ox helps users leverage data to refine their analytical frameworks over time and to scale proven frameworks across the enterprise. Ox also helps identify future opportunities for automation that can relieve overburdened analysts suffering from data overload while preserving the essential qualities of human judgment. The resulting output optimizes human-led analysis and helps train ML algorithms to improve intelligent decision-making at scale. The Ox tool is designed for users with no modeling or data science skills, building on existing MCDA methodologies in an intuitive, interactive interface. Ox is easy to learn, easy to teach, and requires no special equipment or software. It can be used alone or collaboratively, and used quickly to meet tight deadlines. Ox works on a range of analytical and decision-making challenges, both within and outside of the Defense ecosystem.  With Phase II funding and AFWERX support, Ox will help USAF analysts and other decision-makers make high-quality judgments, faster, by powering proven analytic techniques with AI. To meet this goal, Ox’s Phase II effort will accelerate development of the web-based Ox platform, working with Analysis & Exploitation Teams (AETs) within the 480th Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance Wing. Our Phase II effort will ensure that AETs can leverage Ox’s customizable frameworks to conduct structured, rigorous, and consistent analysis and integrate AI and ML models directly into their workflows.","Ox: Analytical and decision support tool enabling human-machine teaming"]

column23: ["AI Powered Tech Scouting & Recommendation Engine","Congress and DoD recognize that small businesses are critical to the US economy and our national defense. Yet DoD spends an astonishing 31.7% of its contracting budget with just 5 large defense contractors and over 63% with the top 100 defense contractors. There are 10M plus small businesses in the US. DoD engages only a tiny percentage of them. Unfortunately, there presently is no effective way for DoD to identify and engage the overwhelming majority of NDCs or to evaluate the value they can provide to DoD or the threat their technology could present if used by a state or stateless enemy. DoD requires a platform to effectively identify, evaluate and engage nontraditional defense contractors that can deliver game changing technology to DoD and the warfighter to ensure capability advantage and mission success.  Third Coast Federal's AI Powered Tech Scouting and Recommendation Engine (\"Recommendation Engine\") is the solution.   Our existing commercial tech scouting and market research platform, the Federal Navigator, includes a data lake of structured and unstructured data regarding 2M+ businesses, many of which are nontraditional defense contractors (NDCs). Currently, users search for innovators by keywords or Natural Language Processing (NLP) phrases, with the ability to filter by geographic location, NAICS codes and other factors. As good as keyword and NLP search tools are, they are an inefficient and imprecise means for evaluating DoD problem statements and ranking industry capabilities. Searches often return many hundreds, or even thousands, of innovators. As a result, identifying innovators with the precise capabilities required to solve a particular operational or sustainment problem remains a labor intensive process.   For this STTR, Third Coast Federal, Inc. and the University of Notre Dame are enhancing our Federal Navigator tech scouting and market research platform to create an AI Powered Recommendation Engine that leverages knowledge graphs and deep neural nets to instantaneously evaluate DoD needs and simultaneously identify pools of industry and faculty innovators with the technologies and capabilities required to solve identified needs. In Phase I, our team established the technical feasibility of using knowledge graphs and neural networks to produce recommendation algorithms that achieve accurate need comprehension, as well as candidate capability identification, scoring and matching. In Phase II we are developing a prototype Recommendation Engine MVP to help the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center and its constituents engage AI innovators to solve operational and sustainment challenges with AI powered solutions. The MVP solution will employ machine learning and utilize HITL (Human in the Loop) feedback from diverse subject matter experts to provide domain specific refinements to the Recommendation Engine to improve accuracy and performance.","F2-14589 ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE POWERED TECH SCOUTING & RECOMMENDATION ENGINE"]

column23: ["CALIBRATION OF ETHICAL TRUST FOR LETHAL AUTONOMOUS WEAPONS (CETLAWS)","Calibration of Ethical Trust for Lethal Autonomous Weapons (CETLAWS)","This proposal is for Phase II continuation of our project to develop a software framework for Calibration of Ethical Trust for Lethal Autonomous Weapons (CETLAWS) that can be used by Air Force, other DoD organizations and commercial enterprises. The mission impact of this project on the Department of the Air Force will be an enhanced understanding of the roles of ethics and trust in lethal autonomous systems and the availability of new methods to facilitate calibrated trust in human-autonomy teaming scenarios. Ethical trust calibration will increase military users’ willingness to collaborate with lethal robotic technology and will also overlap with key commercial applications in trusted artificial intelligence (AI) and social computing. In Phase I of the present project, we demonstrated and validated an initial CETLAWS using a simulation of a swarm of autonomous lethal unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and a set of ethical equations for making autonomous Shoot/No-Shoot decisions. In Phase II we will implement a complete CETLAWS prototype using both ethical equations and Bayesian modeling for trust calibration, validate this prototype; and begin our transition and commercialization activities with an initial focus on insertion into DAF wargames and test events with the help and collaboration of our USMC end-user."]

AF21S-TCSO1, PROPOSAL FX21S-TCSO1-0356 STTR PHASE I - MACHINE LEARNING APPROACH FOR OPTIMIZING REAL-TIME ORBITAL SENSOR TASKING","The Space Force urgently needs to accelerate space-asset tasking in the wake of adversarial threats. column23: ["Efficient Search and Rescue (S&R) of personnel is critical for providing lifesaving care during combat and natural disasters (e.g. floods, hurricanes, earthquakes, etc.). Current S&R practices have significant technical challenges including: (1) information used for determining subject locations and safety risks is often incomplete, error prone, contradicting, and/or out of date, (2) search procedures are sub-optimal due to vast search areas and/or unique domain constraints/obstructions, with high dependence on the search domain (i.e. combat, lowland, mountain, urban, cave, or maritime), and (3) dynamic environments such as threat movements, weather, and flood water runoff, significantly impact the performance of sensors and scene understanding algorithms. The RAISR technical solution interfaces with the next generation C2 (Command and Control) systems and UxV (Unmanned Vehicle) platforms to address these technical challenges, by: (1) integrating automated scene understanding and low-level planning cues onboard manned/unmanned assets, allowing for undisrupted operations in dynamic, low-communication environments, (2) performing data fusion and high-level planning at mobile command stations for further determining of safety/threat risks, optimizing overall search plans, and identifying safe rescue paths, and (3) incorporating human-in-the-loop features for adding human knowledge to the system, providing human explanations, and options for human adjudication of any automated decisions. RAISR follow-on work aims to enable lightly trained teams to deploy domain-configured toolboxes with pre-packaged UxV platforms, sensors, and algorithms, while interfacing with mobile command station C2 systems and humans-in-the-loop. The future deployed RAISR solution is expected to have an order of magnitude improvement in the following four areas: reduction of search/rescue times, increase in percentage of successfully rescued personnel, improvement of S&R worker safety, and reduction of S&R equipment cost to maximize scalability. ","RAISR (ROBUST ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR SEARCH AND RESCUE)","RAISR (Robust Artificial Intelligence for Search and Rescue)"]

column23: ["AUTOMATED RUNWAY SITUATIONAL AWARENESS AND ALERTING","Automated Runway Situational Awareness and Alerting","Thrust AI, in partnership with MIT Lincoln Labs, proposes to research and develop a proof-of-concept system architecture leveraging machine learning and modern extra-visual spectra sensing to accomplish real-time air traffic control (ATC) detection, recognition, and observation of aircraft in the terminal environment. The STTR Phase I effort will determine the technical feasibility, to the maximum extent possible, by which an automated optical system may perform ATC observational tasks in place of traditional (“out-the-window”) gear confirmation, safety observer/chase ship spotting, and pattern monitoring. The solution proposed herein would provide unprecedented situational awareness—fusing optical, radio, and ADSB sensor inputs to provide the decision-maker “human-in-the-loop” with an automated, multispectral, and slewable feed of tower-controlled aircraft beyond the capability of the human eye. Sensor inputs to the computer vision model will encompass the visual, infrared, and thermal spectra to provide hyper-observation capability in low-visibility environments (night, weather, etc). Advantages over the current “out-the-window” model include automation of ATC observational tasks and sensing beyond the human eye (extra-visual spectra, resolution at far distances, and proximity to aircraft). Delivery of real-time advanced analytics furthers the AF S&T Strategic Capability of Rapid, Effective Decision-Making. Sensors clusters will be hosted on the airfield to ascertain a more complete situational picture of the runway environment—further aiding safety and accident investigation boards to prevent aviation mishaps."]

column23: ["ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE LEGAL ASSISTANT","Artificial Intelligence Legal Assistant (AILA)","The objective of the proposed work is to create an analysis software that judge advocates can use to find discrepancies and areas of legal concern quickly and accurately within targeting packages during use-of-force decision-making. The AI Legal Assistant (AILA) will be trained to scan targeting packages to identify discrepancies between images and their human-generated captions for specific Air Force use cases. Customization possibilities for Phase II include ensuring objects (e.g., planes, vehicles, etc.) match in both detail (i.e., color, model, etc.) and use (e.g., civilian vs. military); detecting human bias and assumptions in labeling (e.g., “combatant” vs. “military-aged male” or definitions like “military outpost” which have clear legal definitions); civilian damage estimation / proportionality (e.g., an image labeled as a “field” has different civilian implications if it is an agricultural field vs. a sports field); and collateral estimation (e.g., confirming whether potential dwellings are in the strike zone). If successful, AILA will increase the speed and accuracy of legal review and ultimately improve U.S. targeting outcomes."]

column23: ["ATAK (ANDROID TACTICAL ASSAULT KIT) WOUND DETECTION GARMENT WITH MESH ENABLED RADIO MODULE","ATAK Wound Detection Garment with mesh enabled radio module","The 147th Air Support Operations Squadron (ASOS) is a proven strategic partner with an innovation mindset focused on supporting the tactical air control party (TACP) and United States Air Force (USAF) enterprise. The 147 ASOS is part of over 5,000 Texas Air National Guard members supporting active duty, global state partnership programs, and state humanitarian missions. 147 ASOS/TACP have a unique set of capabilities that afford them the ability to conduct search and rescue efforts, border security, and joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) responsibilities. This requires them to often be positioned on the forward edge of the battlespace subjected to hazardous conditions dislocated from a main operating location. These operators and leaders need resilient, effective, and survivable technologies capable of empowering Agile Combat Employment (ACE) initiatives to overcome anti-access, area denial (A2AD) environments. Legionarius (teaming with goTenna) will create a solution that can be used to organize, train, and equip Airmen with technology that can save lives by providing near real-time awareness of Airmen health through AFRL's Team Awareness Kit (TAK), including at the edge or in off-grid environments. The Legionarius ôSmart Garmentö (i.e., uniform or Wound Detection Shirt) is capable of detecting vital signs and penetrating wounds to the warfighter (shot, shrapnel, cut, burn), autonomously sending out an alert via Android Tactical Assault Kit (ATAK) and the Air Force Battlefield Assisted Trauma Distributed Observation Kit (BATDOK) system for instant casualty reporting and tracking. The system automatically and instantly provides the following information to the relevant parties: How many casualties? Who specifically is injured? What type of wound? What are the current (and historic) vital signs? Where and When did the injury occur on the battlefield? Problem: Currently, the only way to identify if a warfighter has been injured is through traditional verbal communication methods or input via typing into information systems. Both efforts require human-in-the-loop actions. Opportunity: The Smart Garment can sense vital signs and penetrating impact to the body (shot, shrapnel, cut, and burn), and can autonomously send out an alert via ATAK, BATDOK, and the Armyĺs Medical Hands-free Unified Broadcast (MEDHUB) system using goTennaĺs Pro X mesh radio networks. Sending this alert gives medics a head start and to reduce the time from point of injury to point of treatment. Legionariusĺ Smart Garment can provide the ability to transmit critical information through mesh networks for near real-time decision making. Legionarius will enable the USAF to have instant knowledge of injury, including GPS location, location on the body, current and historic vital signs, and other critical information that displays on ATAKĺs Common Operating Picture (COP)."]

column23: ["TIGHTLY COUPLED INTEGRATION OF THE FIELD OPS REMOTE TRACKER (FORT) INERTIAL TRACKING MODULE WITH A COMMERCIAL OFF THE SHELF GLOBAL POSITIONING SYSTEM RECEIVER TO CREATE AN EXTREMELY ELECTRONIC WARFARE RESILIENT TRACKING DEVICE","TIGHTLY COUPLED INTEGRATION OF THE FIELD OPS REMOTE TRACKER (FORT) INERTIAL TRACKING MODULE WITH A COTS GPS RECEIVER TO CREATE AN EXTREMELY EW RESILIENT TRACKING DEVICE","The Ukrainian and Israeli wars have emphatically clarified that EW directed at GPS vulnerabilities will be a persistent part of battlefield calculus.á As weapon platforms shrink in size and cost and are able to grow in numerical advantage as a result of this SWaP-c transformation, the only viable defense that is effective on a consistent and economical basis is EW, where large swaths of air space can be covered by just a few EW installations.á On the other hand kinetic mitigation can not only miss the threat, but costs far more in operation and can also cause inadvertent collateral damage.á Because of such battle-proven efficacy, EW will inevitably receive the manpower and financial investment to continue evolving into ever more sophisticated and difficult to detect, mitigate and defeat methods and technologies. The proposed deviceádelivers unprecedented fully self-contained GPS-denied tracking capability using only magnetometers, accelerometers, gyroscopes, and a pressure sensor.á With PNI Sensor's sensor fusion algorithms and Edge AI/ML models, its tracking performance surpasses that of an inertial navigation system based upon tactical grade gyroscopes and accelerometers but does so using only COTS consumer-grade MEMS accelerometers and gyroscopes.á Therefore, it enjoys the benefits of extremely low SWaP (< 1 cubic inch and <100mW in operation).á Combining the FORT with a commercial GPS unit using a very tightly coupled approach would enable both EW-proof location as well as more generally accurate and reliable positioning performance of the GPS receiver even when GPS is fully available.á Signal processing would not have to be solely constrained to RF signals (except for rudimentary pose information provided by inertial sensors in some existing systems), but can pull location, velocity and pose into increasingáthe efficacy of the GPS filter substantially.","Tightly Coupled Integration of the Field Ops Remote Tracker (FORT) Inertial Tracking Module with a COTS GPS Receiver to create an extremely EW resilient Tracking Device"]

column23: ["Pepr","THE WORK PLAN INCLUDES DISCOVERY, CONTINUOUS DEPLOYMENT OF SECURITY SERVICE INTEGRATION (PEPR), INTEGRATION OF MISSION APPLICATIONS WITH COMMON SECURITY COMPONENTS USING PEPR, AND A FINAL REPORT DOCUMENTING  THE PROPOSED EFFORTS AND CONCLUSIONS.","The objective of this program is to address the critical need for advanced cybersecurity integration within the Department of the Air Force (DAF), specifically catering to the needs of the 90th Cyberspace Operations Squadron and Platform One. This automation is expected to enhance the scalability of cybersecurity capabilities across the Air Force and Space Force, enabling the deployment of modern defensive and offensive cyber capabilities across the entire DAF. Pepr’s adaptability also allows it to operate effectively in air-gapped and disconnected environments, a key requirement for DAF operations. The technical volume of the proposal outlines the integration process, key milestones, and expected outcomes, demonstrating Pepr’s potential to revolutionize cybersecurity practices within DAF and its suitability for broader commercial application. The implementation of Pepr addresses a fundamental challenge within DAF – the integration of mission-critical applications into secure platforms. By reducing the total time and expertise required for integration, Pepr enhances the operational efficiency and security of DAF systems. Its ability to operate in diverse environments, including air-gapped scenarios, further underscores its utility for defense applications. The successful deployment of Pepr is poised to significantly improve the cybersecurity posture and operational readiness of DAF units, making it a pivotal tool in the modernization of defense cybersecurity infrastructure."]

Flight Optimal utilizes artificial intelligence-driven algorithms, data analytics, optimization techniques, and a cloud-based architecture to deliver scalable, accessible and optimized daily training schedules to flight schools. Data integration: integration of optimization engine, native database (aircraft, facilities, instructors, and students), and existing databases and data management systems. The result is a responsive schedule and robust reporting and analytics capability able to assess performance of training programs, resource utilization, and compliance with regulatory and operational requirements. Real-time adaptation to changing scheduling priorities, unscheduled events (driven by aircraft, training facilities, instructors, or students), and weather. Human-in-the-loop control: review and edit an optimized schedule before publishing and making it available to users. This added level of control allows schedulers to modify the scheduling solutions based on last-minute information and even manually recreate a schedule if needed.??????? column23: ["AETERNUM NEXT GENERATION SENSORS: ENABLING WEATHER INTELLIGENCE FOR TACTICAL SUPERIORITY BEHIND ENEMY LINES","Aeternum Next Generation Sensors: Enabling Weather Intelligence for Tactical Superiority Behind Enemy Lines","Weather events such as typhoons and heavy rains will play a pivotal role in any future conflict between the United States and China in the Indo-Pacific region and impact supply chains and logistical capacity of the military. Military sites are also at risk due to weather events as ~1,700 U.S. military sites throughout the world are located on coastlines valued at over $100 billion subject to rising sea-levels.  Regardless if it is dropping bombs, performing space or airborne intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR), or delivering cargo, weather impacts all aspects of Dept of the Air Force (DAF) operations. Tactical and precise weather awareness is a key element of mission success. Weather is a crucial factor as air strike planners in the combined air operations center (CAOC) calculate how to mitigate collateral damage and how to ensure survivability of the aircrews. Owning the weather is now more than ever important with new computer modeling tools, enhanced high-resolution satellite imagery, and reach back communications. Aeternum’s modular (ability to measure varying combinations of different sensing variables using unique cartridges) design allows for the measurement of mission-critical weather variables continuously and the flexibility to determine which variables need to be measured for a given mission. Being the most cost-effective (50x cheaper while still providing accuracy and the ability to measure singular or multiple variables at once or in a network), attritable, modular sensor in the market, Aeternum can be left behind in contested environments making them an ideal choice for all weather teams part of the 9th Operations Group and AFSOC. The Aeternum weather sensors can be built to specifically address the needs of the weather team whether they are sensing singular parameters or the suites are stand alone or part of a network. Aeternum aims to accomplish in this Phase II: 1) determine the feasibility to design a completely modular sensor that includes the potential ability for pressure, temperature, present weather, ceilometry, wind velocity and visibility, 2) design different modules which can go together within one cartridge (suite) or individually added, 3) equip the sensor for communication modularity by expanding on its current cellular and LoRa capabilities, 4) continue to provide appropriate power options based on the environment the sensor is placed i.e., solar/battery and dynamic enough to adjust transmission of data (frequency of data being shared with the controller) based on power option selected, 5) update the design of the sensor to be cost-effective greatly reducing the current price tag of current sensors, 6) provide a prototype for testing of new design and features."]

CONTINGENCY RESPONSE FORCE","Counter-sUAS Passive Detection, Tracking, and Kinetic Kill for Contingency Response Force","     The proliferation of weaponized small Unmanned Aerial Systems (sUAS) is an asymmetric threat to Department of the Air Force (DAF) forces during Agile Combat Employment (ACE) operations.  Especially concerning is the ability of near-peer threats to conduct “Drone in a Box” component to defeat fiber optic and autonomous AI driven sUAS airframes.  The proposed WATCHDOG C-sUAS system directly addresses the Air National Guard’s WEPTAC validated Critical Capabilities gap: “The Contingency Response Force (CRF) lacks the ability to properly secure airfield locations due to the lack of a modernized airfield security detection system and counter small unmanned aircraft system (C-sUAS) kit during wartime situations.”     Trident Sensing will rapidly develop WATCHDOG to meet the CRF’s C-sUAS capability gap.  Existing company commercial solutions will be integrated to produce an austere drone detect and kill system.  WATCHDOG focuses on passive detection and tracking through EO, IR, RF and acoustic means.  Passive sensing allows the system to operate through all levels of Emissions Control (EMCON).  The tube launched PITBULL Low Collateral Effect Interceptor (LCEI) kill vehicle is included to defeat emerging sUAS threats driven manually through an un-jammable fiber optic link or employing AI to navigate and target without an external RF link.  The all-electric kinetic defeat system will operate similar to a Stinger missile out to more than 2KM but without a hazardous rocket motor or warhead.  PITBULL kill vehicles will come pre-packaged in a self-contained tube to enable rapid reloading.  WATCHDOG systems will include detect and track nodes and up to 10 4-round launchers.  Each WATCHDOG launcher will be a node in the detection, tracking and defeat network.  The CRF will “own” the system, but every Airman participating in ACE operations will be able to grab a PITBULL launcher and be part of the counter-swarm solution.  All components will be capable of data sharing across existing CRF Android Tactical Assault Kit (ATAK) situational awareness hardware and software ecosystem.  Growth capabilities include networking launchers to accept cueing from existing garrison style C-sUAS systems.  A well-resourced and fast-paced Phase II development effort will culminate with the production of two prototypes to support End-User evaluations. "]

column23: ["AF22A-T005, F22A-T005-0038, CHARACTERIZATION OF STORE TRAJECTORY DYNAMICS RELEASED FROM INTERNAL CAYITIES","RAPID CHARACTERIZATION OF STORE TRAJECTORY DYNAMICS USING RE","Rapid Characterization of Store Trajectory Dynamics Using Reservoir Computing","The six degrees-of-freedom (6DOF) motion of a store released from an aircraft cavity can be exceedingly complex, especially for vehicles operating at supersonic or hypersonic velocities.  In these conditions, the store must pass through shear flows, boundary layer separation regions, vortices, and turbulence, each of which can alter the trajectory in subtle and unexpected ways.  In extreme cases, the store can fail to separate or reverse course back up toward the aircraft, condition called a “bad launch.\"  It is of great interest to the Air Force to identify the fundamental causes of these trajectory dynamics so that rules can be established for cavity and store designs for the next generation of attack aircraft.  These new fighters, bombers, and remotely piloted aircraft (RPA) will be designed for weapons deliveries at higher altitudes and Mach numbers than their predecessors and will require extensive simulation and testing to validate stores release functionality in the expanded envelope. Current approaches to understanding store trajectory dynamics rely on live-fly observations, wind tunnel tests, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations.  CFD simulations are often the starting point of any design cycle because they do not require building a physical system and reduce the need for repeated experimental trials.  Unfortunately, state-of-the-art (SOTA) CFD simulations usually require super-computer-level resources for generating example launch events and can take weeks of computer time.  And if results are unexpected or undesired (e.g. a bad launch), the required analysis of large amounts of data may reveal no obvious root cause in the conditions that govern store trajectory.  In short, the discrepancies are so small, and the underlying physics so complex, that current data analysis methods cannot determine the signatures of a bad launch. ResCon Technologies, LLC and Clarkson University propose collaborating with the Air Force to explore a pioneering new approach: Machine Accelerated Analysis and Prediction (MAAP), a machine learning (ML)-based solution with the ability to analyze, predict, and generalize the dynamics of a system based on limited CFD results.  MAAP is built on our recent ML breakthrough known as Next-Generation Reservoir Computing (NG-RC) and will rapidly learn cavity/store dynamics to (a) provide a computationally efficient framework for evaluating the effects of various launch parameters, and (b) accelerate the solution of CFD problems.  MAAP will have the power to inform both aircraft design and weapons release control schemes while saving time, energy, and money over current methodologies.  Ultimately, MAAP’s advancements will lower risk to the warfighter, increase lethality, and lead to a greater probability of mission success."]

column23: ["EVOLUTIONARY DESIGN OPTIMIZATION FOR GUIDED WEAPON CONCEPTS","EVOLUTIONARY DESIGN OPTIMIZATION FOR GUIDED WEAPON CONCEPTS MODELING AND SIMULATION","EVOLUTIONARY DESIGN OPTIMIZATION FOR GUIDED WEAPON CONCEPTS MODELING AND SIUMULATION","Evolutionary Design Optimization for Guided Weapon Concepts Modeling and Simulation","When the United States enters conflicts throughout the world, guided weapons that can eliminate threats while minimizing collateral damage are a necessity for all branches of the DoD. Each weapon is designed for a specific mission, though there is no guarantee that the design is either optimized for that mission or robust to mission changes. The scope of the design parameter space and the ever-evolving missions requiring guided weapons make accomplishing one or both tasks extremely challenging for current design practices. As computational power continues to increase, novel optimization methods that efficiently navigate such highly complex, large, multi-disciplinary design parameter spaces and fitness calculation become a more feasible solution to this problem. Evolutionary algorithms mimic natures approach to developing complex systems through generations of design variations and provide a novel means to optimize design. To this end, the team of Systems Technology, Inc. (STI) and the University of Tennessee Space Institute (UTSI) proposes to develop the Design Algorithm Robust Weapon Interface (DARWIN), a design interface that provides a robust, evolutionary multi-objective/multi-disciplinary optimizer, a design and visualization interface, and an architecture that utilizes modeling and simulation capabilities to evaluate the performance and improve the design from one generation to the next."]

column23: ["DEVELOPMENT OF REACTIVE MATERIAL-BASED MUNITIONS","DEVELOPMENT OF REACTIVE MATERIAL-BASED MUNITIONS FOR POL TARGETS","Development of Reactive Material-Based Munitions for POL Targets","The objective of this proposal is to develop a new class of munitions adaptable with hypersonic platforms to provide the Air Force with defeat mechanisms against petroleum, oil and lubricant (POL) facilities along with maritime targets. Strategic POL targets include crude oil wells, pumping stations pipelines, storage facilities and refineries to name a few. Based on the teachings of previous wars on the importance of petroleum products in any nation’s civilian and military infrastructure, advanced military strategies hinge on the tactical defeat of these targets to paralyze our adversaries. While these operations can neutralize an opponent, the strategic stepwise neutralization POL targets with minimal collateral damage is critical to ensure local victory and warfare momentum. As POL and maritime targets are notoriously difficult due to their intrinsic nature, current long range strike weapons fail in efficiency. Based on judicious technology, our proposed weapon system will take advantage of high density and high strength reactive materials (RMs) with a high energy density to enhance target penetration performance and provide incendiary effects capable of exploiting the lower flammability of the POL. While initiating the combustion of these fuels remains challenging in scenarios where collateral effects must be controlled, RM-based systems can be tailored to deliver high sustained temperatures. The proposed structural reactive material (SRM) will consist of alloyed elements capable of participating in an energetic (exothermic) chemical reaction that will radically alter weapons effectiveness, providing a high-performance multi mission air-delivered weapon. These reactive materials have been shown to ignite diesel fuel, burn or deflagrate explosives, and over-pressurize missile airframes and structures."]

column23: ["Imaging seekers have some remarkable advantages over traditional quad cell based laser seekers. The vast increase in information allows for many new capabilities, but current imagers lack the incredibly high bandwidth of quad cell detectors, which has been relied on for target discrimination. In seeking to replace quad cell SAL seekers with imaging SAL seekers, a priority is to first replicate everything a quad cell can do, before exploring the additional flexibility and freedom that comes with full image information. In order to actually get the seeker fielded in a reasonable amount of time, it is preferable to recreate existing methods as closely as possible in order to minimize the required testing. We propose a novel way of integrating the timing and spatial information available with COTS SWIR imagers to closely approximate preexisting LSPL algorithms despite the bandwidth limitation.","PERFECT TIMING IMAGING SEEKER","Perfect Timing Imaging Seeker"]

column23: ["Autonomous Information Processing Benefits to commandONE C2 Capabilities","SBIR PHASE1 : AUTONOMOUS INFORMATION PROCESSING BENEFITS TO COMMANDONE C2","The Air Force (AF) has a need for agile software applications to support the commandONE program, which serves as the Command and Control (C2) component to its Advanced Battle Management System (ABMS). These systems need to accommodate future operational capabilities as well as support and improve utility from legacy Theater Air Control System (TACS) assets. Intelligent Artifacts’ overall Technical Objective for Phase I is to articulate feasibility of our autonomous information processing capabilities and illustrate how our software solution can be leveraged within the commandONE application layer architecture to benefit mission requirements. To this end, specific Technical Objectives of this project are:  1) Show data standardization feasibility among commandONE applications – possible via Intelligent Artifacts’ general data format (GDF),  2) Illustrate integration between ABMS applications, sensors, data libraries, access devices – possible via Intelligent Artifacts’ framework built on loosely coupled layers (data, intelligence, application) and simple API calls,  3) Showcase Verification & Validation (V&V) – possible via Intelligent Artifacts’ explainable information processing system with ability for human-in-the-loop influence to independently test/optimize multi-objective use cases and 4) Illustrate an accelerated path to autonomous persistent-Intelligence Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR)/C2 – possible via Intelligent Artifacts’ solution in a containerized construct embedded at various nodes of the battle management space."]

column23: ["SBIR PHASE 1 : SHIELD AI PROPOSAL","Shield AI Proposal","Shield AI develops artificial intelligence (AI) for multi-agent unmanned systems (UxS) in support of the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD).  This work entails the development of Mission Executive software which enables a collection of aerial effects (UAS) to execute coordinated autonomous behaviors while remaining responsive to the environment and input from the human-on-the-loop.  Shield AI has developed Mission Simulation software that allows a user to efficiently design, develop, test, improve, and implement autonomous capabilities for UAS.  The proposed effort will establish the feasibility of integrating an AI architecture for mission execution, developed and tested in simulation, with an existing UAS.   This proof of concept will enable a conventional UAS to “play back” a reactive mission profile learned in simulation.  The effort anticipates a Phase II objective of achieving online integration of the Mission Executive with an existing UAS using standard interfaces to allow for dynamic, autonomous RSTA mission execution by one or more platforms."]

column23: ["Next generation U.S. Air Force weapons require improved capability to strike targets (relocating and stationary) in Global Positioning System (GPS) denied areas while minimizing collateral damage and fratricide.  The combination of imaging sensors and advanced image processing enable weapons with improved capabilities for navigation and locating and engaging targets.  Uncooled shortwave infrared (SWIR) cameras image in day and nighttime conditions and detect current 1060 nm and future covert eye safe 1500 nm laser designators.  Princeton Infrared Technologies proposes to integrate an uncooled, high resolution SWIR imager with BAE Systems’ Open Seeker Architecture (OSA) for insertion in an Air Force munition for captive carry testing at the end of Phase II.   The OSA is a new cost-effective optical seeker for precision-guided munitions that facilitates integration of new and multiple sensors.  The seeker’s open architecture enables highly accurate, competitive, low-cost munitions to navigate and locate targets in limited-access and denied environments.  This effort lays the foundation introducing advanced targeting capabilities on multiple weapon platforms.","SIBR PHASE 1 UNCOOLED SWIR CAMERAS INTEGRATED WITH OPEN SEEKER","SIBR PHASE 1 UNCOOLED SWIR CAMERAS INTEGRATED WITH OPEN SEEKER ARCHITECTURE","Uncooled SWIR Cameras Integrated with Open Seeker Architecture"]

column23: ["NEXT GENERATION OPEN MISSION PLANNING SYSTEM SMALL BUSINESS INNOVATION RESEARCH (SBIR) PHASE II","Next Generation Open Mission Planning Systems","SMALL BUSINESS INNOVATION RESEARCH PHASE II BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT F212-0008","SMALL BUSINESS INNOVATIVE RESEARCH (SBIR) PHASE II BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT F212-0008, TRANSFER MODIFICATION","The advancement of the Next Generation Open Mission Planning Services (NOMS) architecture requires an Application Programming Interface (API) for the Fly Out Model (FOM). FOMs are a key component of mission planning, more specifically weapons planning, that are provided by weapons manufacturers.  FOM libraries provide the algorithms that produce results such as acceptable regions of weapon release, footprints that represent strikable ground areas, and flyout trajectories from release to target. FOMs are currently provided by different manufacturers with their own software and dependencies. The vision of creating a single gateway API for FOM calculations allows for a single-entry point for all consumers in need of FOM calculation capabilities in their applications.  In our earlier SBIR Phase 1, we researched and developed the initial gateway design along with initial details regarding the creation of what we referred to as a FOM Development Kit (FDM).  The focus of this phase will be to further research technologies that can assist in developing a more open solution to FOM use by engaging further with the mission planning community and FOM manufacturers to develop a microservices based topology architecture that would allow desktop, web, and mobile users easier and scalable access to weapons performance data.    "]

column23: ["CONTEXT AWARE SUPPORT SYSTEM AND INTUITIVE INTERFACES (CASSINI)","Context Aware Support System and Intuitive Interfaces (CASSINI)","For intelligence analysts, rigorous and timely analysis of structured and unstructured data demands efficient collection, integration, exploration, and exploitation of multi-dimensional data, across a range of missions and contexts. Unfortunately, the ability to support these tasks is severely limited by current tools that rely extensively upon costly manual processing by analysts and inefficient workflows for interacting with automated tools. To address these needs and develop improved human-on-the-loop workflows, we propose to design and demonstrate Context Aware Support System and Intuitive Interfaces (CASSINI). CASSINI will combine advanced multi-dimensional information visualizations with deeply integrated collaboration tools and novel reinforcement learning automation to support exploration and reasoning in analyst workflows. First, we will extend upon prior cognitive analyses conducted with intelligence community practitioners to define the requirements for joint analyst-automation teaming. Next, we will design a set of ecological human machine interfaces and collaboration tools within a fusion-oriented streaming analytics workflow environment. Finally, we will extend existing visualization environments to rapidly prototype CASSINI interfaces and workflows. Combined, CASSINI-based support tools will facilitate intuitive visualization, interaction, and teaming with new automated models as part of effective and efficient analyst workflows."]

column23: ["Collaborative military engagements with integrated systems across multiple disparate platforms such as Manned/Unmanned Teaming (M/UM-T) require resilient communications to achieve desired effects against enemy threats. The potential benefit of M/UM-T systems can be fully realized if Command and Control, flight control, shared situational awareness, sensor/electronic warfare, targeting, weapon system and a host of other mission-critical data and information are exchanged with extremely high reliability among all the engaged assets in real-time throughout a mission. Existing tactical communication systems, however, are not well suited to support the M/UM-T requirements nor to exploit the full potentials in a constantly maneuvering environment. We are developing the Resilient Communications for Autonomous and Scalable Manned/Unmanned Teaming with Bounded Autonomy (ReCAST) to address these challenges in a unified framework, and propose to demonstrate its feasibility under realistic M/UM-T scenarios. The goal of ReCAST is to enable all engaged assets with disparate capabilities to exchange just the right amount of information by dynamically and intelligently allocating communication resources between the engaged manned/unmanned assets even when they are under the most pressing situations by enabling individual assets to persistently make the right â€œdecisionâ€� on when to communicate what with whom based on the local and global network status.","RESILIENT COMMUNICATIONS FOR AUTONOMOUS SCALABLE MANNED/UNMANNED TEAMING","Resilient Communications for Contested Autonomous Manned/Unmanned Teaming and Bounded Autonomy"]

column23: ["EXPLAINABLE AND TRANSPARENT MACHINE LEARNING FOR AUTONOMOUS","EXPLAINABLE AND TRANSPARENT MACHINE LEARNING FOR AUTONOMOUS DECISION-MAKING","Explainable and Transparent Machine Learning for Autonomous Decision-Making (EXTRA)","This effort aims to develop interpretable and reliable machine learning methods that address the challenge of deriving explanations of autonomous decision-making behavior. In particular, the proposed effort focuses on the challenges inherent in interactions between humans and intelligent machines, where transparency and trust are essential to facilitate successful human-machine teaming. This effort, based on deep reinforcement learning, will address the fact that autonomous decision-making agents can affect future states based on their current actions, as well as the challenge of reasoning over long-term human-machine collaborative objectives of the underlying mission. The resulting explainable system enables better understanding of learning outcomes, and can also help develop more effective machine learning algorithms.  The developed systems can be applied to military scenarios by enabling human-interpretable behavior explanations in human-in-the-loop decision processes. These systems may also be deployed in commercial applications such as autonomous driving or energy management systems, where high-stakes decisions require transparency and traceability. The proposed explainable machine learning techniques can also be implemented in heavily regulated areas, such as healthcare or financial systems, where stringent interpretability and accountability are required. The objective of this effort is to conduct a feasibility study and validate prototype concepts for future development and integration."]

column23: ["In response to the DoD SBIR 2023.3 Solicitation for the Space Force Phase I Program, topic F233-0014 “Multi-Body Behavior Modeling of Space Systems,” Advanced Space, LLC (Advanced Space) proposes a comprehensive feasibility study applying machine learning (ML) based approaches to investigate and develop tactical-speed analytical capabilities that characterize and assess multiple objects and threats in space. Critical to such applications is an automated intelligence agent (or agents) that can assess real-time data intuitively, make informed and contextual decisions, and recommend the best course of action to a human operator who ultimately decides whether to pursue the recommended action. In other words, we aim to reduce the burden on the human-in-the-loop requirements throughout the entire data analysis process, and strategically automate certain aspects of this process to increase tactical response capabilities.  A fundamental component of ensuring freedom of operation in space is space battle management and command and control (SBMC2), with a core tenet therein being the ability to conduct real-time analysis of the risk to mission. This is necessary to allow action to be taken accurately, knowledgeably, and on appropriate timelines.  Collected data can be used to provide information to form hypotheses, but these hypotheses must have meaningful and critical context for BMC2 decision-making. Traditional approaches to modeling multi-object and/or campaign-level activities is time consuming and labor intensive, carries high levels of bias risk, and does not easily accommodate iteration for comparative and/or “what-if” analysis.  The improved and new capabilities will support more complex analyses on tactically-relevant timelines and enable a robust risk assessment to include likelihood and consequence of events. The technology to be developed will consider multiple behavioral and physics inputs, perform threat and impact analysis beyond single object and event actions, and present assessment results in mission-time for critical decision making.  Ms. Kanak Parmar will be the Principal Investigator (PI) for the proposed project. She has an extensive background in strategic applications of AI/ML algorithms for various phases of standard space mission operations. Ms. Parmar is a Staff Astrodynamics and Satellite Navigation (ASN) Engineer, as well as an AI/ML Engineer, at Advanced Space. Through various projects and prior research, she has experience in applying ML to trajectory station keeping and path planning; robust autonomous optical navigation; soft data characterization schemes; and human-AI cooperative/interactive learning approaches in multi-objective, contextualized, and priority-based situations. She will be supported by Dr. Nathan Ré, Principal ASN Engineer, who is a subject matter expert (SME) in low-thrust trajectory optimization and the use of neural networks for autonomous spacecraft operations. ","MULTI-OBJECT BEHAVIOR MODELING OF SPACE SYSTEMS","Multi-Object Behavior Modeling of Space Systems"]

column23: ["In response to the Department of Defense (DoD) Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) 2023.3 Solicitation for the Space Force Phase II Program, topic F233-0014 “Multi-Body Behavior Modeling of Space Systems,” Advanced Space, LLC (Advanced Space) proposes to apply ML algorithms to create a containerized application that autonomously detects and assesses potential multi-vehicle threats and to remove the need for humans-in-the-loop until decision-quality information is referred to the end-user for final authorization. Critical to this application are automated intelligence agents that can assess real-time data intuitively, make informed and contextual decisions, and recommend the best course of action to a human operator who ultimately decides whether to pursue the recommended action. In other words, we aim to reduce the burden on the human-in-the-loop requirements throughout the entire data analysis process and strategically automate certain aspects of this process to increase tactical response capabilities.  The purpose of this tool is to fit within larger DoD strategic frameworks for Space Domain Awareness (SDA) and constellation Command and Control (C2). The individual components of the tool will be utilized in an integrated software application to containerize the software to be compatible with broader SDA and C2 pipelines. As part of the Phase II effort, Advanced Space will work with Redwire Space, Inc. (Redwire) to better understand the containerization and integration requirements for the software. Redwire has existing expertise in the SDA and C2 realm that will be leveraged alongside Advanced Space’s ML expertise to validate this technology's long-term objectives.  The goal of the proposed Multi-Object Behavioral Modeling effort is to create a software tool to anticipate and mitigate threats to satellites on a constellation scale to defend U.S. and allied capabilities in the event of hostile action against them. Using machine learning (ML) methodologies, the proposed system will define the parameters of potentially threatening maneuvers; perform trajectory analysis to recognize when hostile actions are being initiated; and refer suggested actions to the end-user for final authorization. ","MULTI-OBJECT BEHAVIOR MODELING OF SPACE SYSTEMS - TO CREATE A SOFTWARE TOOL TO ANTICIPATE AND MITIGATE THREATS TO SATELLITES ON A CONSTELLATION SCALE TO DEFEND CAPABILITIES IN THE EVENT OF HOSTILE ACTION AGAINST THEM.","Multi-Object Behavior Modeling of Space Systems"]

column23: ["Machine learning-based Fault Detection, Identification and Recovery (FDIR) software will enable autonomous responses to faults onboard a spacecraft. By removing the human in the loop, anomalies can be addressed quickly, avoiding communication delays and long periods spent in â€œsafeâ€� mode during which the spacecraft cannot perform its mission. There are, however, several hurdles to machine learning-based FDIR, including the diversity of spacecraft and components that require algorithm tuning, the lack of labeled telemetry data from historical missions for training purposes, and the limited amount of telemetry data that includes faults (since anomalies are by definition rare). Verus Research proposes to supplement available satellite telemetry with simulated data to overcome these challenges. We will use unsupervised learning for anomaly detection on real data, and train supervised learning algorithms to classify faults using simulated data. Once deployed, the FDIR software will first detect anomalies and then identify their source. Unidentified anomalies will be studied by operators, labeled, and added to the training data to improve the algorithm, which is re-uploaded to the spacecraft. The entire SBIR effort will culminate in a software deliverable that can be tuned to specific spacecraft and is deployed onboard for use on orbit.","SPACECRAFT FAULT DETECTION IDENTIFICATION&CAUSATION USING MACHINE LEARNING","Spacecraft Fault Detection Identification & Causation Using Machine Learning"]

column23: ["Cambrian Works (CAMBRIAN) addresses a space defense need to execute robotic missions at GEO in the immediate future.  The specific need is for an operator capability to manage operations in real-time at distances as far as GEO (and eventually Cis-Lunar) in a way that the operator can interact with the mission as if truly present at the work site, using open-standards and without “vendor-locked” systems. This solution takes advantage of the Master-Agent relationship within the SRI software architecture to distribute these elements of the control system across end-points within Cambrian’s network that was developed specifically to provide Internet-compatible data delivery and routing for resilient, scalable, low-latency space operations. ","SPACE OPERATOR ROBOTIC TERMINAL AND INTERFACE ENVIRONMENT (SORTIE)","Space Operator Robotic Terminal and Interface Environment (SORTIE)"]

column23: ["ArcSat","BASIC SBIR I AWARD - PROGRAM: ARCSAT","To address the Air Force’s need for better interactions from the presence of end users with supervisory and decision-making roles in contested PNT services, Alluvionic proposes ArcSat, to reduce or eliminate requirements for user PNT interactions for autonomous PNT equipment resilience.  ArcSat is a system designed such that PNT data could not be spoofed or jammed, by using methodologies to analyze received celestial radio frequency (RF) and use Doppler principles and orbital physics to determine exact receiver position with GPS accuracy. By eliminating jamming or spoofing while simultaneously adding PNT sources, ArcSat exponentially increases the effectivity of autonomous PNT systems. ArcSat is an alternative precision PNT for contested and GPS-denied environments using both cooperative and uncooperative RF satellite signals for passive celestial navigation. In this Phase I effort, Alluvionic will design and build an ArcSat simulation model capable of either reducing or completely eliminating human-in-the-loop requirements in contested environments such as tactical edge and hypersonic weapons. Theoretical testing will be conducted with the simulation model. If successful, Alluvionic will develop a plan for future development and prototyping of the ArcSat technology in Phase II."]

column23: ["FEASIBILITY STUDY, SBIR PHASE I, TOPIC SOCOM21C- 001, SUAS MUNITION TEAMING FOR ADVANCED PRECISION STRIKE","KEY PERSONNEL CHANGE","Precision-guided munitions have demonstrated dramatic effects with minimal collateral damage. New technology developed specifically to deny them accurate guidance information is now feasible, even for non-traditional adversaries. Further, digital communications are flooding the air with signals that interfere with communications many guidance methods rely on. Swarms of small, covert small Uncrewed Aerial Systems (sUAS) have the potential to provide accurate guidance information even in challenging environments with unreliable communications and little or no other guidance information. Charles River Analytics proposes to design and prototype Wide Area Targeting Computation for Heterogeneous Engagement and Reconnaissance Swarms (WATCHERS). WATCHERS is a coordination, detection, and guidance capability to identify and designate strike targets, and accurately guide inbound indirect fire munitions using a covert sUAS swarm with automatic target recognition (ATR) and guidance information correction as needed by trilaterating its communication signals relative to each sUAS in the swarm. WATCHERS will run on each sUAS, coordinating actions in a robust, fault-tolerant, and interference-resistant manner using probabilistic reasoning derived from established mission parameters. sUAS in the swarm will localize both the target in 3D space using machine learning (ML) computer vision (CV) algorithms and the munition itself to provide real time navigation data in a fault-tolerant, interference-resistant manner.","RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT CONTRACTS","sUAS Munition Teaming for Advanced Precision Strike"]

column23: ["Compact Efficient LADAR for Target Detection and Ranging","Improved long-range detection, tracking, and discrimination of targets is needed from missiles while in flight. The operational significance in developing this capability is to greatly improve the probability of successful target intercept – providing better target detection, tracking and false-target discrimination than is possible with the currently existing, or even moderately upgraded, on-board sensors. Our solution to this problem is a compact, efficient, functionally-integrated coherent detection ladar subsystem that meets and exceeds the stated customer specifications and adds the capability of precision Doppler which aids in target identification and discrimination. The benefit to MDA of this development effort is the near-term availability of a sensor that can be integrated with future on-board missile sensors, can detect targets to 200 km range, can mitigate interference, can provide very-high-accuracy closing velocity (~ 1 cm/s) and fine range resolution (15 cm) and range precision (~ 1 cm), and is compatible with the harsh missile operating environment. The precision velocity measurement capability of the proposed coherent ladar significantly improves target identification and discrimination and inherently offers additional enhanced measurement modalities including range Doppler imaging. Innovations realized in this development program include the capability to provide target detection at low transmitted peak power compatible with highly-efficient all fiber transmitters, high range resolution and precision. These innovations come via the evolution of a single photon sensitive coherent detection ladar, an efficient high-power Thulium-doped, large-mode-area (LMA) fiber amplifier, wide-band transmitted signal modulation, high-stability programmable reference lasers, and compact and efficient state-of-the art integrated circuits allowing for very compact high-bandwidth signal acquisition and processing. In Phase I, Beyond Photonics (BP) performed trade studies, analysis and modeling, and developed a conceptual design of the proposed ladar. In Phase II we propose to develop a realistic ladar subsystem brass-board and demonstrate that it can achieve the above noted performance in lab and ground-based field testing. Approved for Public Release | 20-MDA-10643 (3 Dec 20)","SBIR/STTR PHASE II R&D","SBIR/STTR PHASE II R&D - COMPACT EFFICIENT LADAR FOR TARGET DETECTION AND RANGING","SBIR/STTR PHASE II R&D COMPACT EFFICIENT LADAR FOR TARGET DETECTION AND RANGING","SBIR/STTR PHASE II R&D EO14042","SBIR/STTR PHASE II R&D-COMPACT EFFICIENT LADAR FOR TARGET DETECTION AND RANGING"]

column23: ["Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) Battle Management for Rapid, Interactive Weapon Selection","SBIR/STTR PHASE I RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT","SBIR/STTR PHASE I RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE/MACHINE LEARNING (AI/ML) BATTLE MANAGEMENT FOR RAPID, INTERACTIVE WEAPON SELECTION","Threat missile systems are evolving in type, volume, and capabilities. Current missile defense programs rely on Kinetic (K) kill weapons and various sensors such as ground-based radars, sea-based radars, and Electro-Optical and Infrared (EO/IR) sensors on aircraft and spacecraft to defend against the evolving threats. Kinetic weapons are limited by available interceptor numbers, engagement volume, and time to intercept potentially limiting the CommanderÆs battle plan options. To increase our defense capabilities, Non-Kinetic (NK) weapons, also known as Directed Energy (DE), will be integrated into the Missile Defense System (MDS). These new NK weapons will bring game changing speed-of-light kill capabilities to the MDS. While NK weapons are game changers, they are not without their own limitations. Weather conditions can degrade NK weapon effectiveness which must be a consideration for the MDS and Commanders in planning and executing engagements. To address this complex battlespace, the Commander will need new tools for situational awareness, weapon selection, and rapid decision aides for real-time assessment and execution. ExoAnalytic Solutions (ExoAnalytic) is proposing an integrated Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Machine Learning (ML) approach that blends the speed and optimization advantages of deep reinforcement learning with the human understandable advantages of probabilistic-based reasoning. The system will be fast and accurate but include the human in the loop in a telegraphic and rapid-feedback manner allowing commanders the opportunity to rapidly assess multiple battle plans updated over time as the battle evolves. Approved for Public Release | 24-MDA-11906 (16 Sep 24)"]

column23: ["GoHypersonic Inc. (GHI) and the University of Dayton (UD) are proposing to the Missile Defense AgencyÆs (MDA) Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) topic Rapid Yaw Maneuvers for High lift-to-drag (L/D) Hypersonic Vehicles. We will investigate a variety of novel control schemes for non-axis symmetric high L/D vehicles which provide the force necessary for rapid yaw maneuvers. These investigations will address the feasibility of the proposed control layouts and establish the required engagement envelope for mission success. The technical problem we seek to tackle is the slower yaw maneuver response times encountered by hypersonic vehicles with non-axisymmetric lifting bodies, in contrast to finned vehicles with conical bodies. Although non-axisymmetric lifting bodies offer the advantage of higher L/D ratios, their yaw maneuver response during bank to turn maneuvers is relatively slow compared to skid to turn maneuvers. As hypersonic technology advances and non-axisymmetric lifting bodies gain prominence, it becomes crucial to optimize their maneuverability without sacrificing the high L/D ratios they offer. Improving the yaw maneuver response times for these vehicles is essential to ensure their agility, mission capabilities, and overall performance. Our proposal aims to develop innovative control surface solutions or hybrid configurations that can effectively decrease the time constant for maneuvers while preserving the high L/D characteristics of the vehicle concepts. By focusing on minimizing the mass, volume, and drag impacts from control surfaces and/or other mechanisms, we shall design solutions that enable yaw maneuvers with time constants comparable to finned cone of similar size. Design and computational studies will allow us to estimate maneuverability and kinetic energy loss during maneuvers at various Mach numbers and altitudes. Based on our findings, we will refine one or two preferred designs that offer improved maneuverability. By addressing these technical challenges head-on, we aim to develop innovative control schemes that enhance the maneuverability of hypersonic vehicles with non-axisymmetric lifting bodies. Our approach combines in-depth research, advanced mathematical modeling, computational simulations, and rigorous performance evaluations. We understand the importance of minimizing mass, volume, and drag impacts, and will prioritize these considerations throughout the design and evaluation process. By advancing beyond the limitations of the cone fin approach and exploring alternative control mechanisms, we aim to provide a leap forward in the field of rapid yaw maneuvers for high L/D hypersonic vehicles. Given our teamÆs combined expertise, research capabilities, and dedication to advancing hypersonic vehicle technology, we are confident in our ability to deliver innovative solutions, rapid design development, and rigorous assessment. Approved for Public Release | 24-MDA-11673 (8 Jan 24)","STTR PHASE I RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT- SOLUTIONS FOR RAPID YAW MANEUVERS FOR HIGH L/D HYPERSONIC VEHICLES","Solutions for Rapid Yaw Maneuvers for High L/D Hypersonic Vehicles"]

column23: ["Antaris TrueTwin: A Cognitive Digital Twin solution for Autonomous Target Discrimination","STTR PHASE I RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT","The proposed R&D project aims to enhance the capabilities of the Antaris Cloud Platform (ACP) and the TrueTwin™ simulation environment to address the specific requirements of the Missile Defense Agency (MDA). Antaris is the pioneering software platform designed to simplify satellite design, simulation, and operations, featuring tools for easy satellite design, advanced digital twinning, comprehensive spacecraft software, and secure space data networking. Utilizing open APIs and open-source software, the ACP ensures seamless integration without vendor lock-in, significantly reducing time-to-orbit by 2X% and constellation lifetime costs by 10X. In this project, we will adapt our commercially developed ACP and TrueTwin™ simulation environment to meet the Missile Defense Agency (MDA) requirements. The ACP integrates three primary modules: the Antaris Design Studio for interactive mission and satellite design, the TrueTwin™ simulation environment for virtual mission testing, training, and wargaming, and the Antaris Command Center for automated, resilient, and secure satellite operations. By leveraging the TrueTwin™ module, we will generate a unique dataset to support the creation of a Cognitive Digital Twin (CDT) capability. TrueTwin™ can simulate a wide range of operational scenarios at scale and on an accelerated timeline, enabling the creation of essential synthetic data currently lacking in operational systems. This data will be produced through multiple TrueTwin™ scenarios, covering diverse operational use cases, thus providing the necessary inputs to enhance missile tracking and threat identification for the MDA. Approved for Public Release | 25-MDA-12052 (27 Mar 25)"]

column23: ["Neoskye proposes an advanced Cognitive Digital Twin (CDT) framework designed for Autonomous Target Discrimination, integrating data from space-based infrared sensors and land based radars. This innovative system addresses the limitations of current missile defense technologies through sophisticated sensor data integration, real-time processing, and adaptive learning techniques. Our CDT framework utilizes Bayesian inference and Monte Carlo simulations to handle sensor resolution differences, coverage disparities, and viewing geometry limitations. This ensures robust data fusion and accurately predicts target behavior under various conditions, such as different weather scenarios and sensor performance variations. Higher-level contextual information is integrated using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and domain-specific ontologies, providing a comprehensive understanding of threat evolution and the environment. We implement edge computing near the sensors, such as land based radars and space-based infrared systems, to optimize real-time data collection and minimize transmission for preliminary data processing. Adaptive data sampling adjusts the collection rate based on threat levels, ensuring efficient bandwidth and resource usage. Reinforcement learning algorithms like Q-learning and Deep Q-Networks (DQN) facilitate continuous model updates, enhancing the system's ability to identify high-priority targets even with incomplete data. Bayesian networks are employed for advanced anomaly detection, ensuring timely responses to potential threats. LSTM networks and Bayesian optimization enable real-time decision-making, reducing decision latency to under one second. Using tools like MATLAB and user feedback platforms, continuous feedback and performance evaluation mechanisms ensure iterative improvements and high reliability. Neoskye’s CDT framework offers a scalable, modular solution, providing significant advancements in missile defense capabilities and ensuring effective and precise target discrimination in complex and evolving environments. Approved for Public Release | 25-MDA-12052 (27 Mar 25)","SBIR/STTR PHASE I RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT: USING COGNITIVE DIGITAL TWIN FRAMEWORK FOR AUTONOMOUS TARGET DISCRIMINATION","Using Cognitive Digital Twin Framework for Autonomous Target Discrimination"]

column23: ["R&D AUTOMATED PROFIT INCENTIVE DETERMINATION (RAPID) STTR PHASE 1","R&D AUTOMATED PROFIT INCENTIVE DETERMINATION (RAPID)STTR PHASE 1","RAPID Phase 1 - Research and Feasibility","Speed and efficiency in unlocking private sector innovation is central to advancing warfighter capability. The current pace of technology transfer between the Department of Defense and small/non-standard innovators increasingly responsible for these critical innovations, however, presents opportunity for improvement. This technology transfer is impeded in part by the manner in which DoD attracts and incentivizes these firms and procures their technologies. For DARPA, a particularly problematic component of the acquisition apparatus is the weighted guidelines method that currently informs negotiations of incentives for efficient contractor performance. Plainly stated: the weighted guidelines method is not effective at quickly and accurately identifying the factors that motivate small and non-standard innovators on the bleeding edge of technology advancement and does not align with the DoD’s increasing reliance on OTA acquisition mechanisms. It is with these considerations in mind that DARPA contemplates the R&D Automated Profit Incentive Determination (RAPID) tool as a potential replacement for the weighted guidelines method. The Avascent/IN3 team will identify and qualify motivating factors that stimulate efficient contractor performance and establish an evaluation model for DoD customers to leverage in assessing those factors. Avascent/IN3 understand that there is a diverse set of factors that impact contractor efficiency and profit targets. We hypothesize these factors range from highly contractor-specific to technology-driven to contractual. With our initial hypotheses in place, we will rapidly leverage secondary and primary research through our proven methodologies and networks to vet and refine these lists of factors and associated variables, enabling us to transition to developing an evaluation construct that includes relative importance of each factor on contractor efficiency, interdependencies between factors, and levers available to DoD to influence each factor. We will then test the efficacy of the motivating factors and evaluation framework through a series of evaluation samples based on distinct contractor types, market sectors, and types of R&D programs to test the applicability of the evaluation construct as a program and customer-agnostic tool. Avascent/IN3 will design a tool that blends automated inputs with guided dialogs and reference points embedded in the tool to support manual inputs. This hybrid approach would automate tedious data entry of readily available information, while also providing the user decision aids within the tool to aid with inputs that require human judgement. During Phase I, Avascent/IN3 will leverage proven and scalable tools, including “low-code” platforms such as Microsoft’s Power Apps and Microsoft's’ robust AI/ML back-bone to quickly develop a capable and scalable RAPID solution for DARPA."]

column23: ["SALSA SBIR PHASE 2, SECURING ANTIQUATED LANGUAGES VIA PROGRAM SYNTHESIS AND HUMAN ASSISTANCE (SALSA) PROGRAM","SBIR PHASE 2 SECURING ANTIQUATED LANGUAGES VIA PROGRAM SYNTHESIS AND HUMAN ASSISTANCE (SALSA)","SBIR PHASE 2 SECURING ANTIQUATED LANGUAGES VIA PROGRAM SYNTHESIS AND HUMAN ASSISTANCE (SALSA) PROGRAM","Securing Antiquated Languages via program Synthesis and human Assistance (SALSA)","We will continue to develop our Phase I translation software for converting legacy C code into Go, building mature software that is practicable and theoretically sound. To demonstrate the maturity of our translation software, we will translate the COBOL compiler GnuCOBOL from C to Go. At a very high level, our Phase II efforts will consist of technical improvements to our lifting tools for program synthesis, along with a new suite of tools for making the translation process more efficient, more robust, and less reliant on user input. Our Phase I efforts were organized around a synthesis engine coded in Rosette, which enables Rosette to view Go code as being punctured periodically with holes, where the holes refer to various patterns of unsafe behavior produced by a baseline “naive” translation from C to Go. The Rosette synthesis engine then uses an SMT solver to fill those holes, replacing the pattern of unsafe behavior with a pattern of safe behavior. Additionally, in Phase I we built a Go utilities library that managed the parsing and translation of Go code into abstract syntax trees into S-expressions and back, to bridge between the raw C code and the finished Go code. Our Phase II efforts will consist of continuing the development of our Phase I synthesis engine, along with improving the automation of the code to reduce the need for human-in-the-loop elements, and improving the verifiability of the translation by automatically generating a large family of test cases. For the Phase I synthesis engine, the areas where our Phase I translation software needs to be especially improved are in handling heap-allocated data and in parsing side-effecting functions. One interesting technical challenge to translating GnuCOBOL from C to Go is that significant portions of GnuCOBOL are written in Yacc (Yet another compiler-compiler), a parser generator. Lifting Yacc to Go will require new tools for identifying ambiguous grammars and lifting Yacc parsers to Go parsers. However, once complete, the translation will serve both as a demonstration of our SALSA translation tools, and as a platform that could lead to future work on translating COBOL."]

column23: ["Cold Weather Injury Simulation System (CWISS)","DHA PHASE II SBIR TITLED: COLD WEATHER INJURY SIMULATION SYSTEM (CWISS)","The predominant approach the Department of Defense (DoD) has used for Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC) training is to develop training that addresses specific injuries and courses of action in the most common environments, including extreme cold environment. When medical training is conducted in extremely cold environments, additional challenges arise with the delivery of care. As expected, there are also training device failures that may need to be addressed since most, if not all, of these training devices are not designed to operate in extreme cold.Ā Ā SIMETRI has developed a haptic PTT and moulage overlay that involved a focus of effort on material research that evaluated the properties and performance of the selected materials that will influence the final construction of prototypes. SIMETRI also developed a complementary Virtual Reality (VR) application, in which a trainee can speak directly with virtual soldiers exhibiting varying degrees of cold weather injuries and impairments while situated in appropriate virtual environments.ĀĀThese interactions are not pre-scripted and do not require a human-in-the-loop, rather the conversation is generated with real-time responses using an informed AI model. Ā During Phase II, SIMETRI proposes to create the Cold Weather Manikin (CWM), a modular manikin with targeted functionality that supports the current and future needs of medical training in extreme and austere environments. The CWM is a targeted fidelity manikin that is designed to perform basic medical functions or procedures while in an extreme cold weather environment. The CWM will replace the use of a low fidelity, non-interactive manikins that only provide the size/shape/weight of a patient and are best suited for procedures such as applying tourniquets or positioning limbs. The VR application will be enhanced as well, adding nonverbal cues, data analysis and learning management, custom voice profiles with affected speech, etc. The moulage overlay will be updated to incorporate more conditions at different stages of progression."]
