column23: ["Consumer vehicles and vessels continue to become increasingly common worldwide, and thus, it continues to be critical for military forces to maintain effective measures to address vehicle-based potential threats. While scenarios with a clear adversarial threat are relatively straightforward to address, situations in which a potential threat’s intentions are unknown can be challenging. In the case where the potential vehicle/vessel-based threat has occurred through a misunderstanding or through circumstances that do not warrant lethal force, kinetic weapons often have undesirable outcomes. Further, the complex nature of modern warfare has led to an increased focus on the use of Non-Kinetic Effect (NKE) to disable an adversary temporarily to reduce casualties as well as the collateral damage to surrounding property. A NKE that disrupts the operation of a vehicle or vessel can provide forces with the additional time and standoff distance necessary to safely establish whether a potential threat is, in fact, hostile without harming the passengers or other persons in the vicinity. The modernization of vehicles and vessels with complex electrical systems creates an opportunity to force a NKE using a High-Power Microwave (HPM) device that bridges the gap between signage, physical obstacles, or barriers and lethal, kinetic weapons. While there are existing systems that can accomplish this goal, these existing systems struggle with size, weight, cost, and range limitations that make them difficult to deploy. Thus, it is desirable to develop a lightweight, compact, low-cost system capable of disabling vehicles in both maritime and ground domains. To address these needs, Integrated Solutions for Systems (IS4S), in concert with Metamagnetics (MTMGX), leveraged the collective expertise of company personnel in HPM/DEW experience to begin the development of a HPM source suitable for disrupting the operation of vehicles and vessels under the previous Phase I SBIR. The Phase I effort has shown significant promise in the ability of the IS4S-MTMGX team to develop a novel HPM source for vehicle and vessel stopping (VVS) applications. The three main tasks of the successful Phase I SBIR are discussed briefly herein for reference, and additional details can be found in the comprehensive Phase I Final Report. The overall objective of the Phase I effort was to explore a novel hybrid approach leveraging IS4S’s Frozen Wave Generator (FWG) technology to generate a low frequency (10-500 MHz) “pump” signal to drive a gyromagnetic Non-Linear Transmission Line (NLTL) designed and built by Metamagnetics (MTMGX) to generate GHz frequency waveforms with some center frequency and bandwidth adjustment. Such a device would provide non-lethal, intermediate force capabilities not only for long-range VVS applications in both maritime and ground domains but as a counter electronics system for a wide range of applications.","Novel High-Power Microwave Source for Long Range Vehicle/Vessel Stopping Applications","R&D: SBIR PHASE II TOPIC N212-101","RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT: SMALL BUSINESS INNOVATIVE RESEARCH PHASE II TOPIC N212-101","RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT: SMALL BUSINESS INNOVATION RESEARCH PHASE II TOPIC N212-101, THE PURPOSE OF THIS ACTION IS TO UPDATE THE CONTRACTING OFFICER REPRESENTATIVE DESIGNATION TO KACIE MILLER.","THE PURPOSE IS TO REMOVE CLAUSE 252.204-7012 AND REPLACE IT WITH CLAUSE 252.204-7012 (DEVIATION 2024-O0013, REVISION 1). column23: ["EMPI is proposing an innovative solution to use a structural reactive material (SRM) projectile launched from an underwater 12GA gun system to neutralize sea mines by a thermally driven reaction.  EMPI has demonstrated a proprietary SRM known as ICEPK shot from a 20mm gun system that can defeat TNT or Comp B mines with low to no collateral damage.  ICEPK survives ballistic launch and initiates on impact with the mine case.  The ballistic impact is critical to create a rubble zone of fractured explosives inside the mine so that the reactive material starts a thermally driven reaction.  The thermally driven reaction consumes all or part of the explosives but more importantly pressurizes and splits the case without detonating.  This will flood any remaining parts of the mine rendering the mine inoperable.  EMPI is teaming with Zero Point to shoot an SRM projectile from their 12GA TiTAN disruptor.  The TiTAN system is electronically fired and TRL 9 as it has been approved and is currently in application with Navy EOD teams.  The eventual CONOPS is to mount the TiTAN system to a ROUV which will navigate to, aim, and shoot the sea mine with the ICEPK projectile.  The low collateral kill of the mine, will enable survival of the ROUV so that it can reengage and visually confirm neutralization.","Expand Lethality of Technologies of Maritime Mining and Mine Countermeasures","FINAL REPORT"]

column23: ["BASE","DIGITAL ENGINEERING - Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML) Hull Mechanical & Electrical Controls","MODIFICATION TO CHANGE THE COR FOR SBIR PHASE II TOPIC N231-028","OPTION I","THE PURPOSE OF THIS MODIFICATION IS TO REMOVE FAR CLAUSES 52.222-21 AND 52.222-26 PURSUANT EO 11246.","To reduce operator burden in monitoring, operating, troubleshooting, and recovering Hull, Mechanical, & Electrical (HM&E) systems on US Navy ships, an autonomous ship domain control system can be employed to deconflict, decompose, and triage tasks in control systems. A ship domain control system that can automatically adapt to changing internal and external environments may improve operation and sustainment of US Navy surface combatants. However, for ship domain control systems to perform well autonomously under significant uncertainties in the system and external environment for extended periods of time, the system must be able to learn and compensate for both internal and external changes in a trustworthy manner without significant external intervention.The Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning Ship Domain Controller effort will address several key challenges necessary to confidently employ artificial intelligence/machine learning within the operation of several interconnected systems that are necessary to meet the mission objectives of the ship. These challenges include, but are not limited to, the sufficiency of the sensor and signal data available on the ship, the rules of engagement between the human operator and the supervisory control system, and the trustworthiness of the commands and actions from the artificial intelligence-based algorithms as they adapt to the changing environment.  Cardinal Engineering and partners Applied Simulation Technologies and Raytheon BBN Technologies will apply proven tools and techniques and develop advanced modeling and simulation capabilities to solve these challenges and demonstrate the solution via a prototypical demonstration in a relevant environment.The products and processes resulting from this effort will demonstrate applicability and scalability of an autonomous, intelligent supervisory control system for US Navy ships and its readiness for land-based testing and shipboard installation and use. Additionally, the products will be positioned for commercial applications in markets requiring improved safety, security, and operational effectiveness, such as industrial controls systems, self- driving automobiles, robotics, and other such control-intensive fields."]

column23: ["ADMINISTRATIVE MODIFICATION FOR STTR PHASE II TOPIC AF20C-TCS01.","AI Powered Market Intelligence & Tech Scouting Recommendation Engine to Drive DoD Discovery and Engagement of an Innovative Industrial Supply Chain","BASE AWARD FOR STTR PHASE II TOPIC AF20C-TCSO1","EXERCISE OPTION YEAR 1","Small businesses are the engine of innovation and job and wage growth in the US. They generate two out of every three jobs added to the economy and over twenty-four percent (24%) of all patents in the top 100 emerging clusters. They also are critical component of the United States Department of Defense (DoD) supply base. The Secretary of Defense recently noted that “[s]mall businesses provide our most creative entrepreneurs and most driven workers.” (U.S. DoD Small Business Strategy, January 2023, p. 4). Nevertheless, over the last decade the number of small businesses in the defense industrial base has decreased by more than 40%. DoD’s inability to identify and engage innovative businesses with the solutions required to empower and protect our warfighters is a matter of national security. We can neither project strength to deter aggression in times of peace, nor protect ourselves and our allies in times of war, if we lack the ability to design, manufacture and deliver the goods required to equip, train, and supply our warfighters at a level that meets or exceeds the ability of our adversaries. One of the key barriers to solving the supply chain issue is DoD’s lack of effective tech scouting and market research tools. Tech scouting and market research are labor intensive processes and current scouting and research tools are incomplete and imprecise. As a result, scouts are often unable to identify the innovative companies, faculty and solutions that are ideally suited to address DoD’s requirements or to paint an accurate picture of the technical landscape. NAVSEA SBIR seeks a solution to facilitate tech scouting, market research and industry engagement to support Navy bespoke requirements in (i) Shipyard and maintenance activities; and (ii) microelectronics (ME). Third Coast Federal’s iScout platform utilizes an AI powered recommendation engine to instantly evaluate DoD requirements against an entire marketplace to pinpoint those providers with the precise capabilities and solutions required to solve the stated challenge. The purpose for the proposed research and development effort described in this Phase II STTR proposal is to fine tune iScout’s recommendation engine, implement robust human-in-the-loop and machine learning algorithms, implement improvements to the knowledge graph (including curation tools), and expand iScout’s data and features to support the Navy’s identification and engagement of innovative teams from industry and academia capable of addressing the Navy’s Shipyard and ME requirements.  Third Coast Federal also will implement a Navy Microelectronics Innovation Ecosystem to support the Navy Microelectronics Strategy, and a Shipyard Innovation Ecosystem to support Navy shipyard maintenance and innovation requirements."]

column23: ["873AUTHORITY","876AUTHORITY","EW Cognitive Tactics, Techniques and Procedures (TTP) Synthesis","Electronic Warfare goals include controlling the electromagnetic spectrum (EMS) by exploiting, deceiving, or denying enemy use of the spectrum while ensuring its use by friendly forces. To support these goals, Triton proposes to further develop NOEMON, a neurosymbolic Cognition-as-a-Service (CaaS), multiagent-based distributed AI system.  The platform will generate machine actionable Electronic support (ES), Electronic protection (EP) and Electronic attack (EA) Tactics, Techniques and Procedures (TTPs) in near real-time against adversary command, control, communications, computers, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (C4ISR). NOEMON supports mission objectives for Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP)-constrained unmanned and/or manned naval platforms. NOEMON is a self-learning system that operates in a self-supervised manner, which starts learning from the existing knowledge corpus of TTPs, CONOPS and EW rules of engagement captured from human SMEs and subsequently computer-encoded by innovative Triton techniques. It then proceeds to contextually learn new TTPs in logical, explainable, and collaborative ways between teams of agents that synthesize not just the TTPs in descriptive language, but the actual source code implementing them"]

TOLLIVER.","NCE","OTHER ADMINISTRATIVE ACTION.","RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT","RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT  \"IGF::OT::IGF\"","SCOPE INCREASE.","Tracking Algorithm(s) for Determining Highest Probability Predicted Intercept Points(s) in the AEGIS Combat System","Vadum will develop and mature the Threat Prediction for Air Defense (TPAD) algorithms which calculate Predicted Intercept Points (PIPs) to support AEGIS Combat System engagements of air defense threats. The TPAD algorithms monitor incoming tracks and compare the tracks to an internal database of threat motion. TPAD predicts the future state of the threat at a desired range from the firing ship based on the similarity of the track to the internal database entries and reports the predicted state as a PIP. The PIP is transmitted to downstream components in order to provide an aiming and guidance solution to the AEGIS Combat System. The use of a PIP-based guidance system decreases the likelihood that an interceptor will spend energy responding to evasive threat motion. The preserved energy can be used either to complete the terminal phase of missile flight or to extend the engagement envelope of a given missile. During the Phase II program Vadum will work with the prime AEGIS contractor and the Government to test the TPAD algorithms against high fidelity threat representations in high fidelity test environments. column23: ["Modernizing Maintenance Operations and Training","PROGRESS REPORT","The Navy is currently experiencing reduced readiness for maintenance operations. Maintenance technicians are not always resourced with all necessary and up-to-date reference documents and have limited access to such documents. AR solutions have currently been applied to training in both military and commercial domains to help bridge the gap. However the current solutions don’t serve as an organic pipeline of training content, don’t store audio/visual remote assistance for future reference, and are limited to a centralized website only. An opportunity exists to develop an AR training solution that captures remote collaboration discourse and permits rapid, human-in-the-loop assembly of expertise sensitive training modules that can be accessed in real time, at the point of need. Design Interactive Inc. proposes the development of Store, Categorize, Analyze, and Transfer Training for Enterprise Readiness (SCATTER), an augmented reality system that extracts potential training content captured from the discourse between a master maintainer and a trainee during a remote-assisted scenario. SCATTER will couple the categorized and analyzed content with geographical positioning (e.g., position relative to equipment) and supportive virtual content overlays (e.g., schematics, animations, etc.) in order to support maintainers of all proficiency levels in increasing their effectiveness and efficiency."]

column23: ["RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT.","SIGnature Management Agent (SIGMA)","USV SIGCON (signature control) consists of enhancing, reducing, manipulating, and directionally controlling all signatures including electromagnetic (EM) and acoustic signatures. USVs will be tasked with a variety of missions from collections to mine clearance, and every situation within every mission demands autonomous, dynamic, real-time onboard SIGCON. This includes the ability to follow International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREGs)/Rules of the Road and Emissions Control (EMCON) as appropriate. We propose SIGMA (SIGnature Management Agent) to autonomously control signatures on USVs. SIGMA takes in potentially days-old broad guidance from a distant controlling station (e.g., mission objectives, commander’s intent, ROE, etc.) as well as organic and inorganic data (e.g., radar, sonar, AIS, GPS, weather) to appropriately control sensors (e.g., turn off active radar, turn ship, broadcast AIS) and employ techniques (e.g., utilize deceptive lighting, spray mist or chaff). SIGMA utilizes several tried-and-tested artificial intelligence (AI) techniques including Knowledge Engineering (KE), Fuzzy Logic (FL), Behavior Transition Networks (BTNs), and Case-Based Reasoning (CBR). Knowledge Engineering refers to the process of extracting knowledge from subject matter experts, developing a Knowledge Representation (KR), and building a system based on formal and informal facts, rules, and frames. Robert Bergman and Jonathan Vandervelde, who have expert knowledge in Electromagnetic Spectrum Operations (EMSO) and Electronic Warfare (EW), will provide subject matter expertise that will be integrated into SIGMA. Fuzzy Logic captures rules that reference qualitative, inexact, or “fuzzy” values such High/Medium/Low. Behavior Transition Networks create intelligent behaviors by dividing behavior hierarchically into tasks connected by transitions. Finally, Case-Based Reasoning (CBR) attempts to solve the current problem by retrieving a previously encountered similar problem and adapting that problem’s solution to the current situation. In Phase I, we will develop a limited prototype SIGMA and test it using both the Navy-provided data and our in-house simulator. In Phase II, we will build at least two SIGMAs with improved capabilities that meet the Unmanned Maritime Autonomy Architecture (UMAA), and we will integrate them into actual USVs."]

column23: ["Management of Intelligent Navigation for Condition-based Ocean Safe Transit (MIN-COST)","RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT","RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT.","Unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) can keep people out of harm’s way, but the unmanned vehicles themselves can become a target or liability. On one hand, our unmanned vehicles must remain covert and avoid the vessels of pirates and hostile nations in open waters. Conversely, in peaceful times or regions, USVs can pose an unintentional risk of collision with non-combatant craft (for example, shipping and fishing vessels). Onboard manned vessels, people can actively make decisions about how exposed or covert the vessel and its crew should be. One solution for USVs is for a remote operator to make those same decisions. However, the very act of communication to a remote operator may increase the USV’s exposure. Therefore, the USV must be allowed to make its own decisions autonomously to manage its signature profile. To address these challenges, Charles River Analytics proposes to develop Management of Intelligent Navigation for Condition-based Ocean Safe Transit (MIN-COST). MIN-COST is an autonomy software tool that uses an adaptive behavior-based approach to actively manage USV signatures to either increase or decrease exposure based on the current situation. MIN-COST will enable a USV to operate in the guidance and constraints previously provided by a remote operator, but will adapt the specific actions based on current reality without relying on real-time operator input or human assistance."]

column23: ["3 - HD-Shape Tether for Autonomous Non-Destructive Inspection Tools","Non-destructive testing and evaluation methods on complex structures for US Naval applications are challenging and labor intensive. Luna Innovations, teaming with the Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI), will develop a 3D free space positional tracking system using Luna’s unique fiber optic HD-Shape technology for autonomous inspection tools. The system will be agnostic to the non-destructive sensor platform and only requires a single reference point for an entire inspection process. It is superior to existing positional systems since it does not depend on multiple encoders that require physical contact with the surface and suffer from error stack-up as the system traverses. In addition, the system does not require precision GPS or line-of-sight. A secondary benefit of HD-Shape is that positional data along the entire length of the tether can be used to identify potential entanglement points in low access or dangerous scenarios and allow for an autonomous system to avoid becoming stuck or damaged.   Luna will collaborate with the Navy and commercial partners to identify the placement of an HD-Shape sensor on robotic non-destructive inspection tool systems. The HD-Shape sensor will integrate into existing platforms utilizing a standardized protocol. Luna has already demonstrated this capability with manual inspection tools by converting HD-Shape positional data to incremental and absolute encoder inputs on a legacy manual inspection system. A completed field system will be capable of positional accuracies and measurement rates better than typical encoder systems. As the system develops it can be coupled to other technologies that use human-in-the-loop feedback like augmented or virtual reality tools. This is especially useful for increasingly complex structures and inspection methods.   To achieve the overall goals, during Phase I, Luna will build a rugged HD-Shape prototype 10 m long sensor for testing and demonstration purposes on a semi-autonomous inspection system at EPRI’s test facilities. The system will demonstrate the capability of being integrated into an existing semi-autonomous inspection system. At the end of the Phase I effort, a prototype sensor including all the necessary hardware and software will be complete and ready to continue development in the Phase II.","SBIR PH 1"]

column23: ["(4) Intelligent Anomaly-Based Maritime Situational Awareness System (IMSAS)","KBSI will establish an Intelligent Anomaly-Based Maritime Situational Awareness System (IMSAS) for enabling intelligent self-contained acoustic detection capability within Unmanned Surface Vehicle (USV) and/or an Unmanned Undersea Vehicle (UUV). The concept is to build a framework for multi-dimensional anomaly detection, where multiple predictive models are trained to model the normative behavior for a taxonomy of pattern types. Advances in deep learning models would be leveraged for calibrating models that are specifically geared for the specific type of pattern and learn the extremely non-linear patterns from noisy data and then use these pattern models to detect indicate unusual situations. The collective capability of these anomaly models will enable optimal autonomous behaviors that can effectively respond to surface ships and submarines. The Phase I project will research, design, and demonstrate the technical feasibility of the IMSAS solution approach. Phase II will refine, enhance, validate, and mature the IMSAS solution for focused sea-based autonomous applications, leading to rapid technology transition and commercialization. Important innovations include (i) taxonomy of pattern types that collectively establish normative behavior, (ii) deep learning, LSTM, and probabilistic graph models that are specifically calibrated for specific patterns, (iii) formulations that enable dynamic and actionable situational awareness for autonomous behaviors.","PHASE I KICK-OFF BRIEFING MATERIAL"]

column23: ["5-Context- and AI-Based Reasoning for Identification onBOard UUVs (5-CARIBOU)","Context- and AI-Based Reasoning for Identification onBOard UUVs (CARIBOU) is a comprehensive, AI-based automatic target recognition (ATR) agent paired with a fundamentally novel reasoning engine. CARIBOU is designed to provide accurate, robust target recognition capabilities that are not easily fooled by novel classes, dim signals, or attempts to deceive, without requiring a human-in-the-loop or burdensome size, weight, and power (SWaP) requirements. The CARIBOU team has already completed some studies under IRAD funding which provide a basis of confidence for the proposed work, demonstrating that off-the-shelf deep neural networks (DNNs) are able to recognize sonar signals at high accuracy. In Phase I, we will expand our work into a full proof-of-concept that demonstrates not only target recognition, but also an ability to reason over the results. This reasoning will improve classification accuracy and identify irregularities such as results with high-uncertainty or indicators of attempts to deceive. Phase I will focus on passive sonar; future phases will consider additional modalities and will include in-water testing using our facilities. CARIBOU is a joint effort between Boston Fusion Corp, which brings expertise in machine learning research for DoD applications, and Advanced Acoustic Concepts, which brings expertise in sonar processing, acoustic modeling, and UxV development.","PHASE I KICK-OFF BRIEFING MATERIAL"]

column23: ["Automated Warhead Characterization System (AWCS)","DE-OBLIGATE","EXERCISE OPTION 0003 & 0004","EXERCISE OPTION CLINS 0005 & 0006.","FULLY FUND CLIN 0001","FULLY FUND CLIN 0003","Mechanical Solutions, Inc.’s (MSI’s) Phase II.5 SBIR Project for the Navy will continue the development and transition of an automated fragment and debris characterization technology, which will be applied to the accurate, time-effective assessment of weapon effectiveness and collateral damage. The DoD and the Navy are interested in enhancements in the technologies through which fragmentation is captured and characterized, which will expand the present test and evaluation (T&E) capabilities for the accurate characterization of warhead fragmentation. In the project’s Base segment, MSI will post-process the image data from debris tests for Naval Surface Weapons Center Dahlgren Division (Dahlgren), in support of the Enhanced Weaponeering and Collateral Damage Estimation Program.  The efficient video image data analyses will enhance various subsequent analyses that are performed, which use as input the processed results of the structure debris tests.  MSI also will develop an automated debris tracking software system for Dahlgren, which will enable the efficient extraction of the debris fragment velocities, trajectories and mass estimates while providing a solution to the shortcomings of manual image analysis for the post-processing of video data from structure debris tests. During Options I and II of the project, the technology development’s focus will shift to the characterization of warhead fragments from Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division (NAWCWD) China Lake.  Since test procedures do not facilitate the direct correlation between certain fragment parameters, uncertainties exist with respect to the warhead Collateral Damage Estimates for the Warfighter. MSI’s further development of the Automated Warhead Characterization System (AWCS) will mitigate the risks which are associated with these uncertainties significantly.  MSI will acquire and post-process the image data from debris tests at China Lake, will advance the existing AWCS software system with enhancements to the algorithms and the user interface, and will introduce upgrades to the AWCS hardware.  MSI’s AWCS will provide expanded and enhanced data acquisition capability, reduced turnaround time, and streamlined operation for the end user, and the software and hardware upgrades which will be made through this effort will enable the transition of a full system to China Lake by the end of the performance period.  The AWCS project will address specific milestones that will provide accurate and cost-effective T&E capability to the warhead test engineers, thereby enhancing the warhead collateral damage estimates, and providing the warfighter with increased targeting opportunities. The AWCS Phase II.5 SBIR Project also will constitute a collaborative effort, since MSI’s performance of the project’s segments will expand on the automated fragment tracking and characterization software algorithms which MSI developed previously for China Lake through the Navy SBIR Program.","POP EXTENSION","RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT"]

column23: ["NGTS-GPT","RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT","SBIR PHASE I UNDER TOPIC N241-011.","The Navy’s Next Generation Threat System (NGTS) is a critical training mechanism for the Navy to ensure its up-and-coming pilots can encounter as many training scenarios as possible to adequately prepare them for the uncertainty of real combat missions.  Knexus proposes to build the framework of NGTS-GPT, a solution designed to harness the power of LLMs with GenAI and speech processing to rapidly and accurately create a multitude of scenarios for aviators to train against along with the automated analysis of Blue pilot communications.  The NGTS-GPT solution that will derive from this research will improve overall pilot efficacy and provide cost-avoidance to the Navy by reducing instructor manpower and human-in-the-loop support requirements.  The proposed NGTS-GPT architecture contains a few different components, designed to explore state of the art GenAI capability to determine the most effective AI capability for this use case.  Knexus has an out-of-the-box plug-in framework for NGTS scenario planning that has previously been used to deploy adaptive agents in NGTS.  We will also leverage our NGTS expertise to build an AI Speech Processer, a component that evaluates Blue communications, and feed the information into our AI Scenario Director.  We will demonstrate the fusion of these capabilities to create individualized training plans for aviators, increasing overall pilot effectiveness."]

column23: ["Method Security proposes adapting and extending its commercial product for the purpose of automated attack path enumeration and hardening in the support of Department of the Navy’s (DON) missions. Method Security builds autonomous security robots that can conduct the work of expert security engineers, pen testers, and red teamers 24/7. The outcome is an enumeration of every attack path and automatic hardening within your security stack. All of this happens within your rules of engagement. Method Security deploys on-prem, in the cloud, at the edge, or fully air gapped to protect the most critical environments and mission systems. This proposed Phase 1 Technical Effort involves taking the Method Security product that has already developed, and conceptually adapting and extending it to  DON-specific connectivity-disadvantaged tactical environments, DON-specific data signals, and DON security objectives. Cyber attacks are about to undergo a great acceleration primarily due to advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI). In the same way that AI developer co-pilots have democratized better coding skills to more novice developers, AI will do the same for hackers. Soon thereafter, malware and other cyber weapons will become partially or completely autonomous. This presents a challenge for Defensive Cyber Operations (DCO) in commercial, government, and military environments alike. Traditional security tooling that is often slow, non-interoperable, and requires significant human operator expertise, already can’t keep up with traditional threats, and stands incapable of a more capable adversary. These more capable adversaries will easily throttle between sophisticated attack techniques vs. trivial attack techniques and fast drive by operations vs. low-and-slow operations. DCO has to outmatch this new adversary, and to do that new autonomous defensive cyber solutions are needed that can predict, preempt, and identify threats at machine-speed. In tactical environments, where data may be unique, the bandwidth is Denied, Degraded, Intermittent, or Limited (DDIL), and compute is constrained, even greater challenges are faced for DCO. The luxury of clean environments and abundance of processing resources is thrown out, forcing operations at the tactical edge to be smarter and self-sufficient. Nation State attackers know of this capability gap at the edge, and will seek to exploit these weaknesses until superior DCO capability at the edge is deployed. column23: ["Digital Engineering – Perception System for Situational Awareness and Contact Detection for Unmanned Underwater Vessels","Highly-contested environments present complex adversary Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance (ISR) networks that target blue surface combatants and main bases in three ways: supporting long-range precision missile attacks, cueing bomber aircraft to attack with cruise and anti-ship missiles at medium ranges, and cueing Surface Action Groups (SAGs) across wide areas of the Pacific. Successful distributed operations require persistent low-cost sensing platforms that can tactically maneuver to provide optimal electronic surveillance (ES) at critical straits, contested island approaches, and in forward sensing areas where SAGs patrol. Over the Horizon Targeting (OTH-T) relies on a variety of long range sensors which are challenged in such a broad theater. Unmanned Surface Vessel (USV) passive sensor employment will provide commanders with persistent sensing providing critical ISR needed for maritime tracking and identification, enhancing sea control and long-range strike. Metron proposes to demonstrate this passive ES capability on the Chesapeake Bay. First by building a single Blacktip USV equipped with an advanced ES sensor, partnered with a second sensor hosted at a Navy Research Lab site on the west shore. These sensors will detect surface emitters of interest and report their parameters to Metron EW track processing and fusion software that will provide an enhanced maritime picture. Metron delivers autonomous UUVs and USVs with industry-leading range, tactical employment, and dynamic payload management utilizing in situ adaptive autonomy. Since its original development over a decade ago, Metron’s Autonomy Navigation Command and Control (ANCC) suite has become the “autonomy of choice” being utilized in the most advanced UUV programs at DARPA, ONR, and PEO USC. ANCC’s proven capabilities consistently deliver real-time, mission planning and pruning without human-in-the-loop—unique to defense and commercial markets, it is deployed on 9 different UUVs. Under an ongoing DARPA project, Metron is providing tracking and fusion processing for an advanced ES sensor reporting a rapid stream of emitter reports. The details of the larger program objectives are classified. However, in April of 2022 over a 1-week period, the prototype ES system was demonstrated in a real-world maritime environment, conducting real-time signal detection, processing, and tracking of multiple bands of maritime radars onboard commercial vessels. The achieved goal was to demonstrate fusion of several bands of track emitters on the same platform for deriving platform-level ID.","RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT"]

column23: ["Helicopter Seat-Integrated Power Assist Device","Myriad studies have shown that the flight environment leads to warfighter fatigue, back pain, and long-term chronic injuries. While recent government investment has sought to address vibration, occupant posture and the weight of body-worn equipment remain prime factors in these issues. Since the 1970s, the weight of equipment loaded on an aviator’s torso has increased by 800% - nearly doubling the total mass supported by the occupant’s lower back. Not only does this significantly increase the chances of acute injuries during extreme events, but the added weight combined with a helicopter pilot’s typical posture leads to an inordinate amount of fatigue and long-term chronic injuries from normal flight operations. To this end, InnoVital Systems has begun developing the lightweight and mechanically safe and simple “ActiveSpine” to off-load the occupant’s spine by providing a secondary “backbone” to transmit the gear loading directly to the seat structure. The ActiveSpine showed improved crash safety in a prior Army program and the Navy Phase I effort redesigned the system for a Navy platform and gear. In the proposed Phase II effort, InnoVital will mature the technology and measure its effectiveness in reducing lumbar musculoskeletal loading through human-in-the-loop testing of a refined system.","RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT"]

column23: ["Automated OMEN Performance Assessment and Analytics Capability (A-OPAAC)","Over the last three years, CPG has built, tested, and deployed a digitized assessment and analytics capability for measuring analyst and planner thinking and problem-solving skills in support of operations in the information environment (OIE). This work has been part of the Operational Mastery of the Information Environment (OMEN) program sponsored by ONR. The developing tool set is known as the OMEN Performance Assessment and Analytics Capability (O-PAAC), a self-contained system built around the OMEN Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scale (O-BARS) that units can use to self-assess individual and team performance across OIE domains, training events, and exercise contexts. As the OMEN program has progressed, the combined capabilities and technologies being developed by various performers are advancing closer to readiness for operational transition to the Fleet. One key area requiring continued focus is the measurement and evaluation component of the OMEN program. Specifically, the theoretical construct underpinning many of the software applications being developed is the BEND Framework (Carley, 2020). BEND is a theory describing the types of influence strategies that go beyond the widely known 4Ds – distract, dismay, distort, disrupt (Nimmo, 2015) – to describe information maneuvers about shaping the narrative and the community of actors. While the current O-BARS applies to any OIE exercise context and is technology agnostic (it can evaluate analyst performance regardless of the specific tools and platforms they are using), a more focused way of assessing BEND performance is needed to support ONR’s objectives for technology transfer. In addition, a stronger, more cohesive, and efficient measurement and assessment capability is needed that blends the power of human-in-the-loop adjudication with the efficiency of automated collection and aggregation of measures of performance in near-real time via automated means. To realize these goals, three lines of research and development must occur. First, the research team must engage with BEND SMEs to build a BEND-specific assessment to gauge analyst and planner performance understanding, using, and applying BEND in their work. Second, the research team must clearly understand, delineate, and articulate the different ways analyst performance in BEND mastery and application can be detected when using OMEN software. This understanding will feed into the construction and validation of an integrated framework that describes what good performance looks like and how development and progression towards mastery is likely to occur when engaging with OMEN software. Third, the research team aims to build prototypes for automating the collection and summarization of analyst and planner BEND performance during OMEN training and exercise contexts. Together, these efforts will advance multiple components of the OMEN program goals while moving towards a self-contained system for measurement and evaluation.","RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT","RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT 873 AUTHORITY"]

column23: ["JACKS: Joint AI-Cyber/EMSO Knowledge System","SBIR PHASE 1.","This proposal addresses topic areas 1 (Artificial Intelligence) and 3 (Cybersecurity).Building on SIFT's experience in cyber-aware Large Language Models (LLMs) and automated planning of cyber attack campaigns, we propose to develop Joint AI-Cyber/EMSO Knowledge System (JACKS) to address three key challenges required to achieve the envisioned Human-AI partnered workflows for Offensive Cyber Operations (OCO):Building scalable OCO planning models: Symbolic AI planning has been used in small, academic-scale demonstrations of planning for cyber operations. Scaling that approach up to realistic environments faces a knowledge-acquisition problem: how to create and maintain symbolic models of all the available sensors and their possible values, actions and their preconditions and postconditions, and goals that might be desired. JACKS will use fine-tuned LLMs to automatically translate the knowledge that is already available in CVE reports, threat intelligence feeds, and other data sources into the AI planning models required to automatically plan OCO campaigns. JACKS will use active experimentation to establish confidence that these planning models are accurate.Creating sound and diverse OCO plans: LLMs alone are not capable of reliably planning OCO campaigns. For example, they can hallucinate actions that do not exist, and they can make fundamental errors in logical and causal reasoning. Furthermore, military operations frequently require planning diverse, alternative courses of action to provide commanders with choices and backups. JACKS will use diverse symbolic AI planning methods to reliably create logical, sound plans that meet an operator's needs, incorporating rules of engagement and other constraints.Helping human operators develop OCO campaigns: Cyber plans, especially those built by automation, can be complex and difficult to understand. JACKS will use LLMs to help with this problem as well, providing a Natural Language interface that can accept goals and constraints from the human operator, explain resulting plans, and implement an operator's requests for revisions, all while keeping in mind prior conversations and context.JACKS will help humans plan OCO campaigns, using LLMs for scalable knowledge acquisition and natural language tasking and interaction."]

column23: ["Accelerator-Based Launcher for Shipboard Systems","LeVanta Tech is developing the HALIA, a first of its kind sea-launched aerial drone.  The HALIA provides a persistent sea-air interface capable of high-speed flight with low detectability.  HALIA fills the gap in current technology.  Aerial drones have limited flight time and cannot stably float on the water.  Even helicopters and seaplanes cannot land on the ocean and float in rough seas. Subsea and surface vessel drones can have endurance but are slow.  The HALIA conserves power while floating and can fly at high speed as needed. The HALIA makes an ideal sea-launched drone carrier.  With a payload capability of 30-40 lbs., the HALIA Group 3 could carry a tube-launched Group 1 UAS (such as the Switchblade® 300 systems).  The HALIA Group 3 can be deployed from a vessel, fly 70+ km, land on the ocean, wait until activated to deploy the Group 1 UAS, and then fly back to the vessel for refuel and reload.  A vessel outfitted with several HALIA Group 3 could maintain a continuous “picket line” of HALIAs 70+ km from the vessel.  The “picket line” of HALIAs can reposition or return to the vessel as the vessel moves.  Beneficially, the HALIA Group 3 can handle the weight and power consumption of SATCOM. The HALIA provides a communication link between the vessel and the launched Group 1 UAS.  Instead of “fire and forget,” the HALIA Group 3 can maintain line of sight communications with the Group 1 UAS, allowing control of the Group 1 UAS from the vessel.  The HALIA can pop-up to low-altitude flight to maintain communications with launched Group 1 UAS.  Additionally, operators have the option to reposition the HALIA as battlespace conditions change.  Furthermore, the HALIA Group 3 can do more than just launch and communicate with multiple small drones.  The HALIA can be configured to carry its own sensor suite and also deploy UUV as well as UAS. The HALIA Group 3 would weigh less than 1,000 lbs. and be deployed from the vessel to the water with a standard davit or crane.   The HALIA Group 3 can collapse to a small footprint when in storage on a vessel but also be quickly assembled with limited manpower and equipment. The assembled HALIA Group 3 would likely be 10-13 feet in length and width, making it suitable for deployment from many naval vessels.A HALIA Group 2 proof of concept prototype is currently undergoing sea trials.  A HALIA Group 3 battery electric version is being developed for the U.S. Air Force.  The Air Force HALIA is designed to persist for at least 30 days in rough seas and maintain enough power to fly and perform vessel target discrimination when activated.  Computational modeling and wind tunnel testing indicate we can develop a hybrid version of the HALIA Group 3 capable of flying over 140 km (to and from the vessel) carrying 30-40 lbs. of payload, land and takeoff from the ocean one or more times, and persist on the ocean as needed.","RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT"]

column23: ["250012 P00001","Hardware-in-the-Loop Simulator with Real-Time Adaptive Scenarios","SBIR PHASE II TOPIC N231-010, ISL PROPOSAL# N2-9034","The Navy has need for realistic threats to exercise advanced electronic combat simulations using their existing Hardware-in-the-Loop (HWIL) capability. column23: ["Collaborative Humanoid Operational Work Robot (CHOWbot)","Our Approach We propose using a robotic humanoid upper torso system of our design, and common kitchen tools in combination with novel control behaviors to perform back-of-the-house duties in an unstructured environment. Our approach represents a significant improvement from state-of-the-art systems, developing a two-armed manipulator system adaptable to the chaotic spaces of the world at a cost equal to or less than a traditional industrial robot. Our Deliverable We propose simulating a two-armed, upper torso humanoid of our Work-Class Perseus effort. We have hardware customers who use our Perseus system for Artificial Intelligence development that would team with our controls effort. Our team would dive directly into controllability studies for the unique and varied tasks and environment of an industrial kitchen. We anticipate that initial tele-operated studies provide proof-of-concept returns which can be de-risked during Phase I before being fully developed into hardware and autonomous behaviors during a Phase II effort. Our concept incorporates and combines previous hardware and controls work of ours in a novel way, allowing a significant impact in modelling and delivering a real-world robotic solution for the chaotic environment of a DFAC. The Rationale Behind Our Approach We have built early prototypes of our Work-Class Perseus Humanoid hardware, but every revision of the system improves the robustness and capability of our already reliable platform. Using this existing platform allows us to focus risk on the execution of tasks instead of the reliability of hardware. We have designed certain foundational control software to match perfectly with our propriety hardware, further reducing the risk pool. This risk reduction allows our controls team to get to work immediately to understand the back-of-house tasks and begin to break those challenges down to a number of simpler behaviors and model, beginning the process of modelling the various tasks from the ground up. Our team would develop a number of strategies in a remote or tele-operation style – proving the path forward to full autonomy during Phase I, allowing us to identify the most powerful, labor-saving, and efficiency improving solutions to take into full autonomy during Phase II. The technical path forward For our path forward, Apptronik in Phase II, will move the control algorithm designs to test and evaluation, shifting from human in the loop tele-operation, to supervision-optional autonomy. We would develop a prioritized function set through end-user dialog and starting with the most significant add autonomy to each behavior in turn down the list.","SBIR PHASE I 20.2, 6 MONTH POP"]

column23: ["Fire control Intelligence and REasoning (FIRE)","PHASE I SBIR","The Army has identified a need for an autonomous fire control system to better protect its soldiers from enemy combatants. However, the rules of engagement are highly dependent on the tactical situation, requiring an autonomous agent to combine context-based information with traditional sensor inputs to make context appropriate decisions. Fire control systems must have high confidence in their decisions, requiring the integration of multiple sources and types of sensor data, confident identification and selection of appropriate targets, and robust target selection according to prioritization schemes and the tactical situation. To meet this need, Soar Technology proposes Fire control Intelligence and REasoning (FIRE), a fire control system supervisory agent that can perform rapid targeting decisions in complex, uncertain environments. Our system will use a cognitive tactical behavior model and knowledge-based reasoning to rapidly fuse data from multiple input sources and select targets based upon the context of the mission, locations of high value assets, and the presence of human team members. Because the need for this system in the field is so great, Soar Technologies will design the system to be quickly integrated with the existing Flexible Fire Control System (F2CS)."]

column23: ["AWARD OF SBIR PHASE 1","Tactical AI Counter Swarm System (TACOS): A Hybrid Machine Learning Approach for Identifying, Classifying, and Defeating Enemy Drone Swarming Attacks","We propose to develop, demonstrate, and commercialize Tactical AI-based Counter Swarm (TACOS) system, a hybrid yet synergistic fusion of expert system and deep learning algorithms in our friendly swarm to identify counter-swarm strategies, track them autonomously with no human control, and defeat them (both kinetically and non-kinetically) with high precision. Current swarm and counter-swarm technologies are experiencing an explosion in the variety of airframes, sensors, weapons (both kinetic and non-kinetic), and control methodologies available for rapid integration and use. As such, deep learning/reinforcement learning approaches to counter-swarm tactics may be invalidated by the rapid integration of new friendly or adversary capabilities. Thus, the technical problem of current swarm and counter-swarm systems is primarily its lack of integration of human expertise (logical reasoning in the form of expert system and ontology) and deep learning; therein exists an unprecedented opportunity to advance the field of counter-swarming technology that exploits the best of both expert system and machine learning. TACOS, with its fusion of expert system and deep learning integration as its core brain for detecting, tracking, and defeating even the most advanced adversary swarms, provides a highly effective, reliable, and explainable system, allowing for assured and bounded behavior and reliable command and control, even with limited, degraded, or intermittent communications. In addition to real-time tactical data (e.g., swarm flight paths), we also consider the swarm behaviors at the operational level which takes into account weapon characteristics, command & control structures, communication types, battery/power-source characteristics, and overall kinetic capabilities. A naïve, pure deep learning-based algorithms will likely fail to establish trustworthy relationship with human operators due to the black-box nature of deep learning algorithms. For Phase I, we will develop and demonstrate our prototype TACOS system as N-vs-M swarm-vs-swarm in a modular, open-system fashion that is capable of: (1) Detecting and classifying adversary swarm behaviors using a combination of swarm flight pattern classifiers and finite state predicate automata (FSPA) which detects swarm tactics; (2) Adapting TACOS responses autonomously to adversary swarm behaviors from (1); (3) Prototyping rapidly and demonstrating TACOS “agents” that actively counter adversary swarm with dynamic, expert-level actions based on ongoing data-stream at both tactical and operational levels, using high-fidelity simulation tools. Specifically, our core Tactical AI technology is designed to allow rapid integration of human-based expert knowledge in order to speed training and convergence to an optimally performing swarm. We anticipate a strong commercialization opportunity by utilizing our SwarmSense product line to readily add TACOS capabilities for both defense and non-defense markets."]

column23: ["ARMY SMALL BUSINESS TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER STTR FOR EFFORT ENTITLED, \"PROTOTYPING OF INTEGRITY-ENABLING GENERIC ESTIMATION MANAGER (IGEM)\"","DARPA SBIR PHASE II CONTRACT FOR EFFORT ENTITLED, \"ION:  A SOFTWARE PLATFORM FOR INFLUENCE OPERATIONS ANALYSIS\"","DARPA SBIR PHASE II FOR THE STATEMENT OF WORK ENTITLED, \"ION: A SOFTWARE PLATFORM FOR INFLUENCE OPERATIONS ANALYSIS","DARPA SMALL BUSINESS INNOVATION PROGRAM (SBIR) FOR THE EFFORT ENTITLED \"ION: A SOFTWARE PLATFORM FOR INFLUENCE OPERATIONS ANALYSIS\"","ION, a proposed software platform for Influence Operations aNalysis, will help an end user uncover adversary or competitor strategy and improve capability to influence target audiences. It will help USG and commercial end users alike answer: What will an adversary or competitor do next and how can I preempt or counter them? Our proposed human-in-the-loop system for anticipating an adversary or competitor’s behaviors will directly enable a new way of carrying out analysis of entities’ events (actions) and communications in context to (a) identify tactics and appropriate counter-measures, and (b) inform a better understanding of strategy. This type of technology, built on methodologically sound frameworks for analysis and proven techniques from the commercial marketing and advertising world, will also provide improved rigor to the influence space, build on best practices, and create an environment for the development of high-quality standards in the field. The principal strength of our proposed technical approach for ION is the incorporation of multiple proven methods that reduce the burden on the analyst. The unique combination of these methods sets the system apart from other tools. In particular, pre-trained language models are revolutionizing the Natural Language Processing (NLP) landscape. ION will leverage these advancements to reduce the amount of input required from analysts and adapt to new domains. Similarly, the proposed techniques for integrated modeling and forecasting leverage proven time series methods with demonstrated efficacy in a wide range of data regimes. These methodological approaches provide a strong foundation for automating large components of the analytical process used in the case studies below. The novel application of state-of-the-art NLP methods is a core component of our technical solution. Large language models have advanced the state of the art in a wide range of benchmark tasks over recent years. Our approach uses these technologies to build a powerful foundation that is further aided by the incorporation of analyst feedback. The combination of these methods is relatively unexplored, particular in the joint analysis of communications and events; however, a large body of literature indicates they hold tremendous promise. A final unique attribute of our technical approach is the way we treat sequences of communications and events as a combined pool of complex signals to detect and forecast behavior. This allows for the application of a diverse set of computational methods to address the integrated modeling and forecasting challenge. Many of these methods have been proven over decades of research, thus minimizing risk. Other proposed techniques are derived from more recent breakthroughs and hold tremendous promise for a revolutionary advancement in jointly modeling communications and behaviors.","ION: A Software Platform for Influence Operations aNalysis"]

THE CURRENT EFFORT CONTINUES THE RESEARCH CONDUCTED UNDER SBIR PH I CONTRACT W51701-23-C-0152.","The U.S. Army faces challenges to operational test (OT) as a growing number of increasingly complex systems become integral to Multi-Domain Operations (MDO). Collecting data from systems under test (SUT) in field conditions that are similar to real-world operational environments has been a staple of OT for many years. However, the amount and types of telemetry and system data from a SUT, as well as the surrounding Live Virtual Constructive (LVC) wraparound, continues to increase. The Army lacks a means to adequately collect and process this data in an expeditious and meaningful way to feed artificial intelligence (AI) models for system test and test data analysis. Current methods require human-in-the-loop data labeling prior to the data being made available to AI/ML applications. The process is expensive, laborious, potentially inconsistent, and time-consuming. The automated system proposed in this paper offers to expedite this process by reducing the personnel required for labeling data. It also provides the opportunity to label the data in near real-time for immediate use in other systems to achieve additional test objectives, system evaluations, and test data analysis."]

column23: ["Army TRUST-LLMOps Enabled Acquisition Requirement Package","EXPRESSION NETWORKS LLC SBIR PHII","SMALL BUSINESS INNOVATIVE RESEARCH (SBIR) DIRECT TO PHASE II, \"AI ENABLED ARP SELECT AND MONITOR\" DEVELOP AND DELIVER STATE OF THE ART AI ENABLED SYSTEM TO MODERNIZE AND AUTOMATE THE ACQUISITION PROCESS STARTING WITH HOW THE ARMY DEVELOPS AN ARP.","This Phase II project solves some key challenges in the Army acquisition requirement package (ARP) including: 1) the manual process of developing acquisition documents according to requirements and templates, 2) the manual process of rewriting/reusing existing documents, 3) the manual process of compliance check and consistent updates across documents, and 4) the lack of access to the most relevant and accurate historical documents and prior examples. Large language models (LLMs) play a crucial role for the Army’s ARP, but their tendency to hallucinate and lack of transparency pose additional challenges to trusted applications.Expression proposes to address these challenges by our innovative solution, Trustworthy, Reliable, Unassailable, Scalable, and Transparent LLM Operations (TRUST-LLMOps), embedded in Visualize, Observe, and React (VOR) artificial intelligence (AI), VOR.AI, an LLM-powered workflow management and accelerator software tool. The Phase II project conducts research and development on the TRUST-LLMOps solution to address reliability and transparency, the two critical aspects of trusted LLM-empowered applications. In addition, it builds a functional prototype of VOR.AI which integrates TRUST-LLMOps with and optimizes it for the Army’s ARP.The anticipated major outcomes of this Phase II project include: i) the TRUST-LLMOps solution framework, algorithms, and engineering processes that ensure the reliability and transparency of the VOR.AI product across a broad set of application areas and customer segments; ii) a functional prototype of the first VOR.AI product tailored to the Army acquisition package; and iii) automated, trusted, and human-in-the-loop ARP workflows with significantly reduced solicitation cycle time and operational cost, as well as improved accuracy and consistency in solicitation documents."]

column23: ["LANGUAGE COMPUTER CORPORATION SBIR DP2","MOD P00002 TO UPDATE TPOC AND DODAAC","MOD P00003 - 4 MONTH POP EXTENSION","Object Recognition of Imagery Entities (ORIENT)","PHASE II AWARD","Under this Phase II effort, entitled Object Recognition of Imagery ENTities (ORIENT), Language Computer Corporation (LCC) will leverage our 20+ years of experience developing ML technologies for commercial and government interests – in such diverse fields as video- and image-based scene analysis, image categorization and decomposition, generative AI, knowledge engineering, and question answering – to develop an interpretable, fine-grained object detection pipeline capable of quickly distinguishing hundreds of different types of objects from diverse visual data sources without the need for extensive annotated training data or human-in-the-loop (HITL). To this end, we will expand upon our existing state-of-the-art image processing technologies to leverage latent object knowledge in support of zero-shot (or few-shot) categorization of detected objects with a focus on electro-optical (EO) satellite imagery, synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite imagery, and ground-based EO and infrared (IR) imagery. We divide our research into four tasks. Under Task 1, we will develop an ensemble of probabilistic and self-supervised techniques to identify all objects in a scene under the “open world” paradigm. This will allow us to cast a wide net at ingestion time and to leverage existing open-source datasets for coarse-grained object detection. In Task 2, we will employ a suite of large language model (LLM) prompts in a multi-stage dialogue to surface fine-grained knowledge of each of the program object-of-interest (OOI) classes for incorporation into a collection of probabilistic object profiles. In particular, we will focus on identifying which features of those objects are likely to be detectable (within a particular imagery type) – including their parts and any visible attributes of those parts (e.g., color, size, shape, material, markings). The features defined in these object profiles will then be exploited under Task 3 to develop a portfolio of lightweight feature detectors trained indirectly using publicly available images via text-to-patch retrieval in a fine-tuned foundational model embedding space. Task 4 will be focused on the fine-grained classification of all detected objects using Pre-Weighted Neural Feature Trees (P-NFTs) that iteratively test an image for relevant features using the Task 3 feature detectors. These P-NFTs, which combine the expressiveness of deep learning models with the explainability of decision trees, will be trained using synthetic feature data constructed by intelligently sampling feature information from the Task 2 object profiles along with features from all imagery data made available in Project Linchpin. We will focus throughout this project on integration and deployability, making sure that all developed software and models can be easily delivered, installed, configured, tested, and deployed within Project Linchpin’s AI Unclassified Operations Environment, as well as other relevant Army and DoD platforms."]

column23: ["RED BALLOON SECURITY, INC, SBIR PH I, TOPIC A244-P057","Targeted Recognition and Analysis of Circuitry Elements (TRACE)","Today, reverse engineering embedded systems – in particular, for the sake of cybersecurity analysis – tends to be prohibitively expensive, primarily because of the amount of expert manual labor and/or very expensive application-specific equipment involved. column23: ["Conflux","Modern tactical environments and enterprise settings alike face the critical challenge of integrating data from heterogeneous legacy systems and modern platforms. In the Department of Defense (DoD) context—exemplified by an Army battlefield scenario—commanders must quickly synthesize information from legacy ground sensor networks alongside modern unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems to achieve unified situational awareness. These disparate systems expose data via various APIs, data models, and messaging formats, often accompanied by incomplete or unstructured documentation. Our proposed approach, Conflux, leverages a multi-agent framework to address these integration challenges. In this context, an agent is a software entity powered by advanced large language models (LLMs) that can autonomously reason, generate code, and interact with data. Agents operate by “tool running”—that is, they invoke and execute external programs or code (for example, in Python or another suitable programming language) to perform tasks such as API calls or data transformation. This language-agnostic “tool running” capability allows the agents to flexibly adapt to different execution environments as needed. The multi-agent framework comprises three specialized roles:Integrator Agent: This agent orchestrates the overall integration process by leveraging chain-of-thought reasoning. It uses a tool-running capability (e.g., a Python execution environment) to dynamically generate and execute code that performs API calls and data transformation routines. For clarity, “tool running” refers to the agent’s ability to call and run code procedures, which may be implemented in Python or another language, to carry out specific tasks in real time.Specialist Agent: This agent ingests API documentation—whether in the form of formal OpenAPI specifications or raw, scraped documents—to extract and understand the key endpoints, data models, and mapping rules required for integration. The Specialist Agent translates these insights into actionable instructions that the Integrator Agent can use.Librarian Agent: This agent curates successful integration and transformation examples by deduplicating entries and maintaining a repository of validated “recipes” that can be reused in future integration tasks. This repository aids in ensuring consistency and reliability as the system learns from each interaction.This dynamic, ad hoc approach avoids rigid data standardization by enabling the agents to normalize and transform data on a case?by?case basis. Although comprehensive security measures and human-in-the-loop monitoring will be further developed in later phases, Phase I will also investigate the feasibility of implementing secure, segregated mechanisms for handling sensitive credentials (e.g., API keys) without exposing them directly to the agents. ","TECHNOLOGY THAT LEVERAGES A MULTI AGENT FRAMEWORK TO ADDRESS INTEGRATION CHALLENGES FACED BY MODERN TACTICAL ENVIRONMENTS AND ENTERPRISE SETTINGS IN LEGACY SYSTEMS AND MODERN PLATFORMS."]

column23: ["Existing C-UAS architectures primarily rely on radar and electro-optical (EO) sensors that are constrained by line-of-sight, generate high power signatures, and are vulnerable to jamming and spoofing. These systems typically require human-in-the-loop operation, increasing cognitive load and delaying response times—especially against swarming or autonomous threats. Near-peer adversaries, including China and Russia, are fielding sUAS equipped with advanced autonomy and sensor fusion, widening the gap between current Army capabilities and emerging operational risks. A scalable, passive, and automated detection layer is urgently needed to protect maneuver forces and critical nodes without compromising mobility or survivability. LAPIS (Low-Altitude Passive Integrated Sensors) directly addresses this capability gap by providing a lightweight, low-size, weight, and power (SWaP), passive sensing system designed for real-time detection, classification, and geolocation of low-altitude threats traveling at variable velocities. LAPIS enables early warning and automated alerting within seconds of threat detection, and can support integration directly with Tactical Assault Kit (TAK) and Army C2 networks (NGC2, FAAD C2, Maven, and Lattice) to streamline operator response.  LAPIS leverages Picogrid’s modular architecture to integrate Guardian RF’s passive RF sensors and Hoverfly’s Spectre tethered UAS (teUAS) into a unified, low-altitude threat detection system optimized for Army use. Guardian RF provides software-defined, passive RF detection and classification capabilities, while Hoverfly’s Spectre platform offers persistent aerial elevation of sensors. Picogrid’s Legion API fuses these inputs—along with EO/IR and acoustic data—into a common threat picture and delivers automated alerts to Army C2 environments. Aligned with the Army’s Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) and designed to support the Army Long Range Persistent Surveillance Program, LAPIS offers a high-impact, low-risk path to expanding the Army’s counter-sUAS capabilities. It reduces the sensor-to-decision latency, minimizes cognitive load on operators, and is purpose-built for mobile operations across multi-domain battlespaces.  Picogrid’s Legion software has been validated in 80+ fielded deployments, with proven ability to integrate and automate workflows for a wide range of sensors. Guardian RF’s detection technology has been used in live operations across U.S. and partner missions, while Hoverfly’s teUAS is widely fielded across the DoD. LAPIS builds on these mature components to deliver a scalable, rapidly deployable capability purpose-built for the Army’s C-UAS mission needs.","Low-Altitude Passive Integrated Sensors (LAPIS)","SMALL BUSINESS INNOVATION RESEARCH (SBIR), DIRECT TO PHASE II, TOPIC A254-027, LOW-ALTITUDE PASSIVE DETECTION SYSTEM."]

column23: ["ARMY MEDICAL RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT SBIR PH I  A181-064-0552, 4 MONTH OPTION","ARMY SBIR 2018.1 PHASE I MEDICAL R&D CONTRACT FOR PROPOSAL A181-064-0552, PROJECT TITLED, AUTONOMOUS RUGGED COMBAT CASUALTY CARE INTERVENTION ARC3-I","Autonomous Rugged Combat Casualty Care – Intervention (ARC3-I)","In the near future, the Warfighter may face prolonged isolation and sustained denial of support on the battlefield, and may have no access to medical support. To become more resilient to these challenges, the Warfighter will need additional, innovative support to provide Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC). Intelligent decision-support software, teleoperated trauma care systems, and fully autonomous trauma care robotics are intriguing solutions. In addition to intelligently diagnosing multiple injuries, performing patient monitoring, and producing prioritized TCCC treatment plans, solutions must assist Warfighters without specific medical training so they can perform interventions. To meet this goal, the solution must interface with telemedical assistance and provide direction to robotic platforms, all within a modular, unified architecture. To address these challenges, we propose to design and evaluate the Autonomous Ruggedized Combat Casualty Care – Intervention (ARC3-I), a modular, intelligent framework for autonomous combat casualty care. ARC3-I combines behavior modeling based on trauma treatment algorithms and procedures with a human-in-the-loop, human-machine interface and robotic adapter, to provide autonomous medical knowledge of interventions that can be performed by either Warfighters without specific medical training or robotic platforms."]

column23: ["Deep Terrain Shaping: Coordinated Effects and Maneuver Using Swarms","In SBIR A244-003 (Deep Terrain Shaping), the Army Applications Lab (AAL) seeks to revolutionize the US Army's terrain shaping process, transitioning from traditional methods to advanced autonomy, AI, robotics, and sensor technology. Novel Engineering, Inc. proposes Coalesce, an autonomous Multi-Agent Command and Control (C2) system, designed to manage terrain shaping operations and includes a collaborative UxV system for detecting and engaging hostile threats. Coalesce is a platform-agnostic system that equips any autonomous vehicle with the ability to collaboratively complete complex objectives. CoalesceÆs core components include a mission planning and monitoring system, a distributed Common Operating Picture (COP), and a custom navigation stack. The system is fully distributed, every platform has all the components needed to reason over their objectives, their swarm-mates current tasking, and the current situation to decide on their next best action even in comms degraded or denied environments. This is controlled from a custom User Interface allowing an operator to plan, monitor, and update swarm activities enabling the swarm to operate at machine speed with human-in-the-loop approving all lethal action. Envisioned to function as the C2 for a comprehensive system of systems, Coalesce operates across extensive battlefield areas, up to 150km ahead of the Forward Line of Troops (FLOT). It utilizes long-range sensors to detect movement and threats. Large carrier Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) deploy small UAS and UGVs deep into the battlespace upon threat identification. These deployed units, equipped with lethal and non-lethal effectors, execute tasks including detection, identification, engagement, and threat assessment. Ā To enhance Coalesce's capabilities, we propose the following significant upgrades to its COP as well as the creation of new swarm tactics to carry out disrupt and fix terrain shaping operations: A situation module that classifies entities in the COP by hierarchical types and provides additional information like expected movement and capability characteristics. A synchronization module that efficiently compares COPs between swarm agents and updates parts of one or both that are out of date. A distributed track fusion algorithm based on the latest particle filter research to enable more accurate tracks built from multiple sensor sources. New swarm tactics to complete all parts of the terrain shaping operation In Phase 1, our approach includes refining system design by collaborating with the user community to derive mission requirements. This phase will detail the selection of vehicles, sensors, tactics, and algorithms, validated simulations or live demonstrations as appropriate. To do this, we are partnering with L3Harris Technologies, Inc for mentorship and SME support in our process and validation of our proposed approaches. The findings and developments will be comprehensively reported at the end of Phase 1.","SBIR PHASE 1: DEEP TERRAIN SHAPING: COORDINATED EFFECTS AND MANEUVER USING SWARMS"]

column23: ["Autonomous and Remote Fuel Agitation, Filtration & Certification","SBIR PHASE I FINAL REPORT AND PROJECT SUMMARY","The Army’s Autonomous and Robotic Remote Refueling Point (AR3P) requires remote and autonomous agitation, filtration, and certification of aviation fuel to execute fueling missions with no human-in-the-loop and still meet all fuel delivery requirements, such as those in ATP 3.04.94 and ATP 4.43. FTL’s “Autonomous Filtration, Agitation, and Certification Technology (AFACT)” uses Commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) and Government-off-the-shelf (GOTS) technology to achieve autonomous and remote fuel agitation, filtration and certification. AFACT is engineered to meet size, transportability, component availability, and engineering simplicity goals that are optimized for the AR3P application. Similarly, AFACT uses no proprietary system interfaces or other design elements that complicate modification, adaptability, and lifecycle optimization as part of the larger AR3P system. AFACT represents a three-part solution that combines simple, safe, standards-based fuel handling technologies to autonomously provide certifiably clean and dry fuel as part of the AR3P system."]

["Autonomy Standards and Ideals with Military Operational Values (ASIMOV)","Title: Autonomy Standards and Ideals with Military Operational Values (ASIMOV)                                                                -       5.000      22.000
Description: The Autonomy Standards and Ideals with Military Operational Values (ASIMOV) program will develop autonomy
benchmarks to objectively and quantitatively measure the ethical readiness of future autonomous systems and the ethical difficulty
of proposed use-cases in support of military operational values (e.g., international humanitarian law, rules of engagement, etc.) in
increasingly complex and changing scenarios. In order to accelerate the development and eventual use of ethical autonomous
systems, an implementable measurement and benchmarking framework of military autonomy must be developed. Based
on technologies developed in the Urban Reconnaissance through Supervised Autonomy (URSA) program (budgeted in PE
0602702E, Project TT-04), ASIMOV's benchmark will enable future autonomous systems that undergo the intensive testing to be
evaluated and scored with autonomy readiness levels (ARL) much like how technology readiness levels (TRL) and manufacturing
readiness levels (MRL) are used to describe the maturity of technology and manufacturing processes, respectively. ASIMOV will
decompose the five Department of Defense's Responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI) Ethical Principles (Responsibility, Equitability,
Reliability, Traceability, and Governability) in a structured, observable, and independently verifiable manner to measure the
readiness of specific autonomous systems to perform ethically within those scenarios. Technology developed under ASIMOV will
be transitioned to the demonstration and operational testing (DT/OT) community, the Director of Operational Test and Evaluation
(DOT&E), and the Services.

FY 2024 Plans:
- Develop initial autonomy benchmark through decomposition of quantifiable values for the five Responsible AI Ethical Principles.
FY 2025 Plans:
- Develop initial framework for the quantitative benchmark.
- Develop ethical and complex scenarios for benchmarking Autonomous Weapon Systems (AWS).
- Develop synthetic data in various sensor modalities.
- Enhance the generative environment to be capable of rapidly generating synthetic scenes and scenarios.
